P 1.loc: Below the collarbone, toward the shoulder: in the 1st space between the ribs, 6 cun from the midline, 1 cun below the hollow under the outer end of the collarbone.
P 1.act: Front-Mu point of the Lung: opens the chest, calms coughing and breathlessness.
P 1.fn: Descends and disperses Lung Qi, stops cough and wheezing, clears Lung Heat and transforms Phlegm; unbinds the chest.
P 1.locp: On the anterior chest, level with the 1st intercostal space, lateral to the infraclavicular fossa, 6 cun lateral to the anterior midline (1 cun below LU 2).
P 1.ind: cough; asthma and shortness of breath; fullness and oppression of the chest; chest pain; thick or purulent sputum; sore throat; nausea and difficulty swallowing; shoulder and upper back pain
P 1.ci: Never needle deeply or medially (risk of pneumothorax): insert obliquely toward the lateral side, 0.5 to 0.8 cun.

P 2.loc: On the anterior chest, in the depression of the infraclavicular fossa, medial to the coracoid process of the scapula, 6 cun lateral to the anterior midline.
P 2.act: Disperses and descends Lung Qi, clears Lung Heat and calms cough; moves Qi in the shoulder.
P 2.ind: cough; asthma; oppression and Heat in the chest; chest pain radiating to the back; sore throat; shoulder pain; inability to raise the arm
P 2.ci: No deep or medial needling (lung, axillary vessels): insert obliquely toward the lateral side, 0.5 to 0.8 cun.

P 3.loc: On the anterolateral arm, just lateral to the border of the biceps brachii, 3 cun below the anterior end of the axillary fold.
P 3.act: Clears Lung Heat, cools Blood and stops bleeding, descends Lung Qi; settles the Po (corporeal soul).
P 3.ind: nosebleed; coughing of blood; cough and asthma; sadness, weeping, forgetfulness; somnolence; dizziness and blurred vision; goiter; pain of the inner arm
P 3.ci: Moxibustion is classically contraindicated at this point.

P 4.loc: On the anterolateral arm, just lateral to the border of the biceps brachii, 4 cun below the anterior end of the axillary fold (1 cun below LU 3).
P 4.act: Descends Lung Qi, regulates Qi and Blood in the chest and relieves pain.
P 4.ind: cough; shortness of breath; chest oppression; pain over the heart; dry retching; agitation; pain of the inner arm

P 5.loc: In the elbow crease, arm straight and palm up, on the thumb side of the large biceps tendon.
P 5.act: Clears Lung Heat, makes Qi descend, transforms phlegm.
P 5.fn: Clears Lung Heat and descends rebellious Qi, transforms Phlegm, regulates the water passages; relaxes the sinews of the elbow.
P 5.locp: On the anterior elbow, on the cubital crease, in the depression lateral (radial side) to the biceps brachii tendon.
P 5.ind: cough with yellow or thick sputum; asthma; coughing of blood; sore throat; afternoon fever; fullness of the chest; acute vomiting and diarrhea; frequent urination or enuresis; elbow pain and contraction; childhood convulsions

P 6.loc: Front of the forearm, 7 cun above the wrist crease, on the line joining LU 5 to LU 9.
P 6.act: Xi-Cleft point of the Lung: calms acute coughs and asthma.
P 6.fn: Descends Lung Qi, clears Heat, stops bleeding and relieves acute conditions; opens the pores to induce sweating.
P 6.locp: On the anterolateral forearm, on the line connecting LU 5 with LU 9, 7 cun above the palmar wrist crease.
P 6.ind: coughing of blood; acute cough and asthma; sore throat; hoarseness, loss of voice; fever without sweating; headache; hemorrhoids; elbow and forearm pain

P 7.loc: On the thumb edge of the forearm, 1.5 cun above the wrist crease, in the small hollow just above the bony bump (radial styloid).
P 7.act: Helps Lung Qi descend and spread, expels Wind, frees the head and neck.
P 7.fn: Promotes the dispersing and descending of Lung Qi, releases the exterior and expels Wind; benefits the head and nape, regulates the water passages and acts on the Conception Vessel (Ren Mai).
P 7.locp: On the radial edge of the forearm, 1.5 cun above the palmar wrist crease, in the groove between the tendons of abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis, just above the radial styloid. Quick guide: with the hands interlocked at the thumb webs, the tip of the index finger falls on the point.
P 7.ind: headache and stiff neck; common cold with chills and fever; cough; asthma; blocked or runny nose; sore throat; facial paralysis; toothache; difficult urination, blood in the urine; genital pain; wrist pain and weakness
cats: Opening (confluent) point of the Ren Mai (Conception Vessel), paired with KI 6
Command point of the head and nape

P 8.loc: On the anterolateral forearm, 1 cun above the palmar wrist crease, between the radial styloid process and the radial artery.
P 8.act: Descends Lung Qi, stops cough and wheezing, benefits the chest and throat.
P 8.ind: cough; asthma; chest oppression and pain; sore throat; fever without sweating; wrist pain
P 8.ci: Needle while avoiding the radial artery. Moxibustion is classically contraindicated.
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Lung

P 9.loc: In the wrist crease on the thumb side, in the hollow just beside the radial artery (where you take the pulse). Press gently.
P 9.act: Yuan-Source point of the Lung: tonifies Lung Qi and Yin.
P 9.fn: Tonifies Lung Qi and Yin, transforms Phlegm, descends Lung Qi; promotes circulation in the vessels and regulates the pulse.
P 9.locp: On the anterolateral wrist, at the palmar wrist crease, between the radial styloid process and the scaphoid, in the depression on the ulnar side of the abductor pollicis longus tendon (just radial to the radial artery).
P 9.ind: chronic cough; asthma; shortness of breath and weak voice; profuse sputum; dry throat; spontaneous sweating; palpitations and chest oppression; weak or barely palpable pulse; coughing of blood; wrist pain
P 9.ci: Needle while avoiding the radial artery (palpate it and push it aside with a finger).

P 10.loc: Halfway along the 1st metacarpal (the thumb bone in the palm), where the skin of the palm meets the skin of the back of the hand.
P 10.act: Clears Lung Heat, soothes the throat.
P 10.fn: Clears Lung Heat, benefits the throat, descends rebellious Qi; harmonizes the Stomach and Heart.
P 10.locp: On the palm, radial to the midpoint of the 1st metacarpal bone, at the border between the palmar and dorsal skin (red and white skin).
P 10.ind: sore, dry throat; hoarseness, loss of voice; cough with blood; acute asthma attack; fever; chest pain; childhood nutritional impairment (Gan); heat and pain of the palm
P 10.ci: Sensitive point: perpendicular insertion of 0.5 to 0.8 cun. Moxibustion is classically contraindicated.

P 11.loc: At the corner of the thumbnail, outer side, 0.1 cun from the corner of the nail.
P 11.act: Soothes a sore throat and clears Heat.
P 11.fn: Clears Heat and expels Wind-Heat, benefits the throat, restores consciousness.
P 11.locp: On the thumb, radial side of the distal phalanx, 0.1 cun from the radial corner of the nail (where the lines of the radial border and the base of the nail meet).
P 11.ind: sore, swollen throat; acute tonsillitis; high fever; cough; nosebleed; loss of consciousness, heatstroke; childhood convulsions; mental agitation; contraction and pain of the thumb
P 11.ci: Painful point: shallow insertion (0.1 cun) or bleeding. Moxibustion is classically discouraged.
cats: One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

GI 1.loc: On the index finger, radial side of the distal phalanx, 0.1 cun from the radial corner of the nail.
GI 1.act: Clears Heat and reduces swelling, benefits the throat, restores consciousness.
GI 1.ind: sore, swollen throat; toothache of the lower jaw; fever without sweating; loss of consciousness, heatstroke; tinnitus, deafness; swelling below the jaw; numbness of the fingers; shoulder pain radiating to the supraclavicular fossa
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Large Intestine

GI 2.loc: On the index finger, in the depression distal to the radial side of the 2nd metacarpophalangeal joint, at the border between the palmar and dorsal skin.
GI 2.act: Expels Wind and clears Heat, reduces swelling and relieves pain of the mouth, teeth and throat.
GI 2.ind: toothache; sore throat; nosebleed; runny nose; facial paralysis; red, painful eyes, blurred vision; fever; shoulder and back pain; pain and stiffness of the index finger
cats: Sedation point of the Large Intestine

GI 3.loc: On the back of the hand, in the depression radial and proximal to the 2nd metacarpophalangeal joint.
GI 3.act: Expels Wind and clears Heat, benefits the teeth, throat and eyes; regulates the intestines and dispels fullness.
GI 3.ind: toothache; sore throat; eye pain; nosebleed; borborygmus and diarrhea; fullness of the chest; fever; pain and swelling of the back of the hand and fingers

GI 4.loc: Back of the hand, between the 1st and 2nd metacarpals, at the midpoint of the 2nd metacarpal on the thumb side.
GI 4.act: Expels Wind, relieves pain, frees the face and head. With LR 3 (the Four Gates): moves Qi and Blood.
GI 4.fn: Expels Wind and releases the exterior, regulates sweating, relieves pain and frees the channels; benefits the face and sense organs (eyes, nose, mouth, ears), moves Qi and promotes labor. Combined with LR 3 (the Four Gates), it moves Qi and Blood and calms the Shen.
GI 4.locp: On the back of the hand, between the 1st and 2nd metacarpals, on the radial side of the midpoint of the 2nd metacarpal.
GI 4.ind: frontal headache; toothache; sore throat; blocked nose, rhinitis, nosebleed; facial paralysis; common cold with chills and fever; absent or excessive sweating; pain in general; painful or absent periods; prolonged labor; hand and arm pain
GI 4.ci: Contraindicated during pregnancy (promotes contractions). Avoid strong stimulation in very weak patients (risk of fainting).
cats: Yuan-Source point of the Large Intestine
Command point of the face and mouth

GI 5.loc: On the posterolateral wrist, at the radial end of the dorsal wrist crease, distal to the radial styloid, in the hollow of the anatomical snuffbox (thumb raised).
GI 5.act: Expels Wind and clears Heat, calms the Shen, frees the channel and benefits the wrist.
GI 5.ind: frontal headache; red, painful, watery eyes; toothache; sore throat; tinnitus, deafness; agitation, incoherent speech; wrist pain and weakness

GI 6.loc: On the posterolateral forearm, on the line connecting LI 5 with LI 11, 3 cun above the dorsal wrist crease.
GI 6.act: Opens and regulates the water passages, expels Wind and clears Heat; benefits the ears, eyes and nose.
GI 6.ind: edema, especially of the face and upper body; difficult urination; nosebleed; tinnitus, deafness; red eyes; toothache; sore throat; forearm pain
cats: Luo-Connecting point of the Large Intestine

GI 7.loc: On the posterolateral forearm, on the line connecting LI 5 with LI 11, 5 cun above the dorsal wrist crease.
GI 7.act: Clears Heat and toxicity, reduces swelling, relieves acute conditions; calms the Shen and regulates the intestines.
GI 7.ind: swollen, painful face; boils and abscesses; sore throat; toothache; inflammation of the mouth and tongue; borborygmus and acute abdominal pain; agitation, inappropriate laughter and incoherent speech; shoulder and forearm pain
cats: Xi-Cleft point of the Large Intestine

GI 8.loc: On the posterolateral forearm, on the line connecting LI 5 with LI 11, 4 cun below the cubital crease.
GI 8.act: Regulates the intestines, expels Wind, frees the channel and relieves pain.
GI 8.ind: abdominal pain; borborygmus; poor digestion; headache; dizziness; eye pain; elbow and forearm pain; paralysis of the upper limb

GI 9.loc: On the posterolateral forearm, on the line connecting LI 5 with LI 11, 3 cun below the cubital crease.
GI 9.act: Regulates the intestines, frees the channel and relieves pain of the upper limb.
GI 9.ind: borborygmus; abdominal pain; difficult urination; hemiplegia; numbness and pain of the arm; shoulder pain; elbow pain

GI 10.loc: On the thumb side of the forearm, 2 cun below LI 11.
GI 10.act: Tonifies Qi, soothes the arm and helps digestion.
GI 10.fn: Regulates Qi and Blood in the channel, frees the collaterals and relieves pain; harmonizes the Stomach and intestines; strengthens Qi.
GI 10.locp: On the posterolateral forearm, on the line connecting LI 5 with LI 11, 2 cun below the cubital crease.
GI 10.ind: pain, weakness or paralysis of the arm; shoulder pain; lateral elbow pain (tennis elbow); hemiplegia; abdominal pain; diarrhea; vomiting; toothache and swollen cheek; fatigue

GI 11.loc: Elbow bent, at the outer end of the elbow crease, halfway between LU 5 and the bony bump of the elbow.
GI 11.act: Clears Heat, cools the Blood, eliminates Dampness, calms itching.
GI 11.fn: Clears Heat, cools Blood, eliminates Damp-Heat, expels Wind and relieves itching; regulates Qi and Blood and benefits the sinews and joints.
GI 11.locp: On the lateral elbow, with the elbow flexed at 90°, at the midpoint of the line connecting LU 5 with the lateral epicondyle of the humerus (lateral end of the cubital crease).
GI 11.ind: fever; sore throat; red, painful eyes; eczema, hives, itching; acne; abdominal pain, diarrhea, dysentery; hypertension; dizziness; pain and paralysis of the arm and elbow; hemiplegia
cats: Tonification point of the Large Intestine
One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

GI 12.loc: On the posterolateral elbow, above the lateral epicondyle, anterior to the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus (about 1 cun above and lateral to LI 11).
GI 12.act: Frees the channel and collaterals, relaxes the sinews and benefits the elbow.
GI 12.ind: elbow pain; stiffness and contraction of the elbow; difficulty bending or straightening the arm; numbness of the arm; lateral epicondyle pain; shoulder pain

GI 13.loc: On the lateral arm, on the line connecting LI 11 with LI 15, 3 cun above the cubital crease.
GI 13.act: Regulates Qi and Blood, frees the channel, transforms Phlegm and dissipates nodules.
GI 13.ind: elbow pain and contraction; arm pain and numbness; inability to raise the arm; swollen neck glands (scrofula); cough; coughing of blood
GI 13.ci: Needling is classically prohibited (Ling Shu); moxibustion is preferred. If needled, avoid the vessels and the radial nerve.

GI 14.loc: On the lateral arm, just anterior to the border of the deltoid, 7 cun above LI 11 (on the line connecting LI 11 with LI 15).
GI 14.act: Frees the channel and benefits the shoulder and arm, transforms Phlegm and dissipates nodules, brightens the eyes.
GI 14.ind: shoulder and arm pain; inability to raise the arm; stiff neck; swollen neck glands (scrofula); goiter; red, painful eyes; visual disturbances

GI 15.loc: On the shoulder, in the depression between the anterior end of the lateral border of the acromion and the greater tubercle of the humerus: with the arm abducted to horizontal, it is the anterior of the two hollows that appear.
GI 15.act: Expels Wind-Dampness, frees the channel and benefits the shoulder joint; expels Wind and relieves itching of the skin.
GI 15.ind: shoulder pain and stiffness; inability to raise the arm; frozen shoulder; weakness or paralysis of the arm; hemiplegia; hives, itching; goiter

GI 16.loc: On the shoulder, in the depression between the acromial end of the clavicle and the spine of the scapula.
GI 16.act: Frees the channel and benefits the shoulder, moves Blood and dissipates nodules; descends Qi.
GI 16.ind: shoulder and upper back pain; difficulty raising or rotating the arm; swollen neck glands; goiter; coughing or vomiting of blood; chest pain from Blood Stasis
GI 16.ci: No deep needling, especially in thin patients (risk of reaching the apex of the lung): insert slightly laterally and downward, 0.5 to 1 cun.

GI 17.loc: In the anterior neck, level with the cricoid cartilage, just posterior to the posterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
GI 17.act: Benefits the throat and voice, transforms Phlegm and dissipates nodules.
GI 17.ind: sore, swollen throat; sudden loss of voice; difficulty swallowing; sensation of obstruction in the throat; goiter; swollen neck glands; cough
GI 17.ci: Shallow needling (0.5 to 0.8 cun), avoiding the neck vessels.

GI 18.loc: In the anterior neck, level with the upper border of the thyroid cartilage (Adam's apple), between the anterior and posterior borders of the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
GI 18.act: Benefits the throat and voice, calms cough and wheezing, transforms Phlegm and dissipates nodules.
GI 18.ind: cough with copious sputum; asthma; sore throat; hoarseness, sudden loss of voice; difficulty swallowing; goiter; swollen neck glands; hiccups
GI 18.ci: Do not needle deeply or medially (carotid artery): shallow needling only.

GI 19.loc: On the upper lip, directly below the lateral margin of the nostril, level with the junction of the upper third and lower two thirds of the philtrum (level with GV 26).
GI 19.act: Expels Wind, opens the nose and stops nosebleed; frees the collaterals of the mouth.
GI 19.ind: blocked nose; runny nose; nosebleed; nasal polyps; loss of smell; facial paralysis, deviated mouth; lockjaw

GI 20.loc: In the groove running from the nose down to the mouth, level with the middle of the nostril.
GI 20.fn: Opens the nose, expels Wind and clears Heat; benefits the face.
GI 20.locp: On the face, in the nasolabial groove, level with the midpoint of the lateral border of the ala of the nose.
GI 20.ind: blocked nose; loss of smell; allergic rhinitis, sneezing; runny nose, sinusitis; nosebleed; nasal polyps; facial paralysis; itching and swelling of the face
GI 20.ci: Moxibustion is classically contraindicated (face). Insert obliquely or transversely upward, 0.3 to 0.5 cun.

E 1.loc: On the face, directly below the pupil (eyes looking straight ahead), between the eyeball and the infraorbital margin.
E 1.act: Expels Wind, clears Heat, brightens the eyes and stops tearing.
E 1.ind: red, swollen, painful eyes; tearing in the wind; poor night vision; nearsightedness; blurred vision; twitching of the eyelid; facial paralysis
E 1.ci: For experienced practitioners only: with the patient looking up, gently push the eyeball upward, insert slowly along the orbital margin with no rotation or lifting-thrusting; press after withdrawal (bruising is common). Moxibustion is contraindicated.

E 2.loc: On the face, directly below the pupil, in the infraorbital foramen (a small hollow felt about 1 cun below the eye).
E 2.act: Expels Wind, clears Heat, brightens the eyes and benefits the face.
E 2.ind: red, painful eyes; itchy eyes; tearing; twitching of the eyelid; facial paralysis; facial pain (trigeminal neuralgia); headache and dizziness; blocked nose
E 2.ci: Do not insert deeply into the infraorbital canal (risk to the nerve and eye): 0.3 to 0.5 cun. Moxibustion is discouraged (close to the eye).

E 3.loc: On the face, directly below the pupil, level with the lower border of the ala of the nose.
E 3.act: Expels Wind, frees the collaterals of the face, reduces swelling and relieves pain.
E 3.ind: facial paralysis; facial tics and spasms; facial pain; toothache; swelling of the cheek and lips; blocked nose, nosebleed; visual disturbances

E 4.loc: On the face, 0.4 cun lateral to the corner of the mouth.
E 4.act: Expels Wind, frees the channels and collaterals of the face, benefits the mouth.
E 4.ind: deviated mouth (facial paralysis); drooling, excessive salivation; tics and spasms of the lips; facial pain; toothache; speech difficulty

E 5.loc: On the face, anterior to the angle of the mandible, in the depression anterior to the masseter attachment, over the facial artery.
E 5.act: Expels Wind, reduces swelling and relieves pain of the jaw and teeth.
E 5.ind: lockjaw; facial paralysis; toothache of the lower jaw; swollen cheek; pain and stiffness of the jaw; spasms of the lips; mumps
E 5.ci: Needle while avoiding the palpable facial artery.

E 6.loc: On the face, one finger-width (middle finger) anterior and superior to the angle of the mandible, on the bulge of the masseter when the teeth are clenched.
E 6.act: Expels Wind, frees the collaterals, benefits the jaw and teeth.
E 6.ind: toothache; facial paralysis; lockjaw, difficulty chewing; jaw joint pain; swollen cheek, mumps; stiffness and pain of the neck; clenched teeth
cats: One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

E 7.loc: On the face, in the depression between the midpoint of the lower border of the zygomatic arch and the mandibular notch (the hollow fills in when the mouth opens).
E 7.act: Benefits the ear and jaw, expels Wind, frees the collaterals and relieves pain.
E 7.ind: deafness; tinnitus; ear pain and discharge; toothache; lockjaw, jaw joint disorders; facial paralysis; trigeminal neuralgia; dizziness
E 7.ci: Locate and needle with the mouth closed; the patient must not open the mouth while the needle is in place. Moxibustion is classically contraindicated.

E 8.loc: On the head, 0.5 cun above the anterior hairline at the corner of the forehead, 4.5 cun lateral to the midline.
E 8.act: Expels Wind, clears Heat, relieves pain and brightens the eyes.
E 8.ind: frontal or temporal headache; heavy head, as if bound; dizziness; eye pain; tearing in the wind; blurred vision; twitching of the eyelid
E 8.ci: Transverse insertion (0.5 to 1 cun). Moxibustion is classically contraindicated.

E 9.loc: In the anterior neck, level with the upper border of the thyroid cartilage, at the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid, over the common carotid artery (palpable pulse).
E 9.act: Regulates Qi and Blood, descends rebellious Qi, benefits the throat and neck, dissipates nodules.
E 9.ind: sore, swollen throat; goiter; swollen neck glands; asthma; fullness of the chest; difficulty swallowing; headache and dizziness; hypertension; vomiting
E 9.ci: Delicate point: push the carotid artery aside with a finger and insert slowly and shallowly (0.3 to 0.8 cun), without strong manipulation. Moxibustion is contraindicated.
cats: Point of the Sea of Qi

E 10.loc: In the anterior neck, level with the cricoid cartilage, just anterior to the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid (midway between ST 9 and ST 11).
E 10.act: Benefits the throat and neck, descends Lung Qi and calms cough.
E 10.ind: sore, swollen throat; hoarseness; cough; asthma, shortness of breath; goiter; swollen neck glands
E 10.ci: Shallow needling, avoiding the carotid artery.

E 11.loc: In the anterior neck, in the lesser supraclavicular fossa, above the sternal end of the clavicle, between the sternal and clavicular heads of the sternocleidomastoid.
E 11.act: Benefits the throat and neck, descends rebellious Qi (cough, hiccups).
E 11.ind: sore, swollen throat; cough; asthma; hiccups; goiter; swollen neck glands; stiffness and pain of the neck
E 11.ci: No deep needling (apex of the lung, large vessels): 0.3 to 0.5 cun.

E 12.loc: In the anterior neck, in the greater supraclavicular fossa, just above the clavicle, 4 cun lateral to the midline (on the nipple line).
E 12.act: Descends Lung Qi, clears Heat from the chest and benefits the throat.
E 12.ind: cough; asthma; fullness and oppression of the chest; pain in the supraclavicular fossa; sore throat; swollen neck glands; shoulder pain radiating to the neck
E 12.ci: Deep needling is contraindicated (risk of pneumothorax and injury to the subclavian vessels): 0.3 to 0.5 cun. Classically contraindicated during pregnancy.

E 13.loc: On the anterior chest, just below the clavicle, 4 cun lateral to the midline.
E 13.act: Descends rebellious Qi, unbinds the chest and calms cough.
E 13.ind: cough; asthma; hiccups; fullness of the chest and ribs; chest pain; coughing of blood
E 13.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: insert obliquely or transversely, never deeply.

E 14.loc: On the anterior chest, in the 1st intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the midline.
E 14.act: Descends Lung Qi, unbinds the chest and calms cough.
E 14.ind: cough; purulent or bloody sputum; asthma; fullness and pain of the chest; rib pain; labored breathing
E 14.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: insert obliquely or transversely, never deeply.

E 15.loc: On the anterior chest, in the 2nd intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the midline.
E 15.act: Descends Lung Qi, unbinds the chest, benefits the breasts; relieves pain and itching of the skin.
E 15.ind: cough; asthma; fullness and pain of the chest; mastitis, swollen and painful breasts; skin painful to the touch; itching all over the body; heaviness of the body
E 15.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: insert obliquely or transversely, never deeply.

E 16.loc: On the anterior chest, in the 3rd intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the midline.
E 16.act: Benefits the breasts, descends Qi, unbinds the chest and calms cough.
E 16.ind: mastitis, breast abscess; swollen and painful breasts; cough; asthma; fullness and pain of the chest; shortness of breath
E 16.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: insert obliquely or transversely, never deeply.

E 17.loc: On the anterior chest, at the center of the nipple (in men, in the 4th intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the midline).
E 17.act: Neither needled nor moxibusted: it serves only as a landmark for the 4th intercostal space and the nipple line.
E 17.ind: no indications for needling or moxibustion; anatomical landmark for locating chest points at the 4th intercostal space (PC 1, SP 18, KI 23, CV 17)

E 18.loc: On the anterior chest, in the 5th intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the midline (below the breast, directly below the nipple).
E 18.act: Benefits the breasts and promotes lactation, unbinds the chest, descends Lung and Stomach Qi.
E 18.ind: insufficient lactation; mastitis, swollen and painful breasts; cough; asthma; chest oppression and pain; difficulty swallowing; rib pain
E 18.ci: Risk of pneumothorax (and, on the left, proximity to the heart): insert obliquely or transversely, never deeply.

E 19.loc: On the upper abdomen, 6 cun above the center of the navel and 2 cun lateral to the midline.
E 19.act: Harmonizes the Middle Jiao and descends rebellious Stomach Qi.
E 19.ind: abdominal distension; stomach pain; vomiting; hiccups; poor appetite; pain of the ribs and hypochondrium; cough and shortness of breath
E 19.ci: No deep needling, especially in thin patients or when the liver or spleen is enlarged (on the right, risk of reaching the liver).

E 20.loc: On the upper abdomen, 5 cun above the center of the navel and 2 cun lateral to the midline.
E 20.act: Harmonizes the Middle Jiao, descends rebellious Stomach Qi and relieves pain.
E 20.ind: stomach pain and distension; vomiting; acid regurgitation; poor appetite; borborygmus; hiccups; vomiting of blood
E 20.ci: No deep needling in thin patients or when the liver is enlarged.

E 21.loc: 4 cun above the navel, 2 cun on each side of the midline.
E 21.act: Harmonizes the Stomach, eases stomach pain, helps digestion.
E 21.fn: Harmonizes the Stomach, descends rebellious Qi, resolves food stagnation and relieves pain; raises Qi and stops diarrhea.
E 21.locp: On the upper abdomen, 4 cun above the center of the navel and 2 cun lateral to the midline (level with CV 12).
E 21.ind: stomach pain; epigastric distension; nausea and vomiting; poor appetite; indigestion, undigested food in the stool; diarrhea; peptic ulcer
E 21.ci: No deep needling in thin patients or when the liver is enlarged.

E 22.loc: On the upper abdomen, 3 cun above the center of the navel and 2 cun lateral to the midline.
E 22.act: Regulates Qi and relieves pain, regulates the intestines and promotes urination.
E 22.ind: abdominal pain and distension; borborygmus; diarrhea; constipation; poor appetite; edema; enuresis

E 23.loc: On the upper abdomen, 2 cun above the center of the navel and 2 cun lateral to the midline.
E 23.act: Transforms Phlegm and calms the Shen; harmonizes the Stomach.
E 23.ind: mental agitation, mania; tendency to stick out the tongue; stomach pain; indigestion; abdominal distension; poor appetite

E 24.loc: On the upper abdomen, 1 cun above the center of the navel and 2 cun lateral to the midline.
E 24.act: Transforms Phlegm, calms the Shen, harmonizes the Stomach and stops vomiting.
E 24.ind: mania, mental disorders; stiff or protruding tongue; vomiting; stomach pain; abdominal distension; diarrhea

E 25.loc: Level with the navel, 2 cun on each side.
E 25.act: Front-Mu point of the Large Intestine: regulates the belly and bowel movements.
E 25.fn: Regulates the intestines, Spleen and Stomach; eliminates Dampness and Damp-Heat and stops diarrhea; regulates Qi and Blood, dissipates masses and regulates menstruation.
E 25.locp: On the abdomen, 2 cun lateral to the center of the navel.
E 25.ind: diarrhea; constipation; dysentery; abdominal pain and distension; borborygmus; vomiting; indigestion; abdominal masses; irregular or painful periods; edema
E 25.ci: Not advised during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy. No deep needling in thin patients.
cats: Front-Mu point of the Large Intestine

E 26.loc: On the lower abdomen, 1 cun below the center of the navel and 2 cun lateral to the midline.
E 26.act: Regulates Qi, moves Qi and Blood and relieves abdominal pain.
E 26.ind: abdominal pain; pain around the navel; painful periods; hernia; lower abdominal distension; diarrhea
E 26.ci: Not advised during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy.

E 27.loc: On the lower abdomen, 2 cun below the center of the navel and 2 cun lateral to the midline.
E 27.act: Strengthens the Kidneys and secures the Essence (Jing), regulates Qi and promotes urination; dispels fullness of the lower abdomen.
E 27.ind: fullness and distension of the lower abdomen; difficult urination; seminal emission, premature ejaculation; hernia; constipation; fright palpitations and insomnia
E 27.ci: Not advised during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy.

E 28.loc: On the lower abdomen, 3 cun below the center of the navel and 2 cun lateral to the midline.
E 28.act: Opens the water passages and promotes urination, clears Damp-Heat from the Lower Jiao, regulates the Uterus and relieves pain.
E 28.ind: urinary retention, difficult urination; edema; lower abdominal distension and pain; painful periods; infertility; lower back pain radiating to the abdomen; hernia; constipation
E 28.ci: Not advised during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy. Have the patient empty the bladder before needling.

E 29.loc: 4 cun below the navel, 2 cun on each side of the midline.
E 29.act: Warms the Uterus and moves Blood: painful, late or absent periods.
E 29.fn: Warms the Lower Jiao, moves Blood and dispels Stasis, regulates menstruation; lifts what has sunk (prolapse).
E 29.locp: On the lower abdomen, 4 cun below the center of the navel and 2 cun lateral to the midline (level with CV 3).
E 29.ind: absent periods; painful periods; irregular periods; vaginal discharge; uterine prolapse; cold in the lower abdomen; infertility; hernia, testicular pain
E 29.ci: Not advised during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy. Have the patient empty the bladder before needling.

E 30.loc: In the groin, level with the upper border of the pubic symphysis (5 cun below the navel), 2 cun lateral to the midline, where an arterial pulse can be felt.
E 30.act: Regulates Qi of the Lower Jiao and the Penetrating Vessel (Chong Mai), descends rebellious Qi, benefits the genitals.
E 30.ind: pain and swelling of the genitals; hernia, testicular pain; impotence; irregular or absent periods; infertility; difficult labor, retained placenta; Qi rushing up from the lower abdomen to the chest; lower abdominal pain
E 30.ci: Not advised during pregnancy. Needle while avoiding the palpated artery; have the patient empty the bladder first.
cats: Point of the Sea of Water and Grain

E 31.loc: On the anterior thigh, in the depression between the upper rectus femoris, sartorius and tensor fasciae latae, on the line from the anterior superior iliac spine to the lateral end of the base of the patella, level with the lower border of the pubic symphysis.
E 31.act: Frees the channel, expels Wind-Dampness and benefits the hip and leg.
E 31.ind: hip and thigh pain; weakness and wasting of the lower limbs; numbness of the leg; hemiplegia; contraction of the thigh muscles; cold and pain of the knee; groin pain
E 31.ci: Moxibustion is classically prohibited at this point (traditional list of points forbidden to moxibustion).

E 32.loc: On the anterolateral thigh, on the line from the anterior superior iliac spine to the lateral end of the base of the patella, 6 cun above the base of the patella.
E 32.act: Expels Wind-Dampness, warms and frees the channel, benefits the thigh and knee.
E 32.ind: pain, cold and numbness of the thigh and knee; weakness and wasting of the leg; hemiplegia; lower back pain radiating to the thigh; weak, swollen legs (beriberi); hernia
E 32.ci: Moxibustion is classically prohibited at this point (traditional list of points forbidden to moxibustion).

E 33.loc: On the anterolateral thigh, lateral to the rectus femoris tendon, 3 cun above the base of the patella.
E 33.act: Expels Wind, Dampness and Cold, warms and frees the channel, benefits the knee.
E 33.ind: cold of the lower back and legs, as if sitting in cold water; knee pain and weakness; difficulty bending or straightening the knee; numbness of the leg; wasting of the lower limbs; pain and cold of the thigh
E 33.ci: Moxibustion is classically prohibited (traditional list of points forbidden to moxibustion), despite its Cold indications; some practitioners still use indirect moxibustion here.

E 34.loc: 2 cun above the upper outer corner of the kneecap.
E 34.act: Xi-Cleft point of the Stomach: calms acute stomach pain and knee pain.
E 34.fn: Harmonizes the Stomach and descends rebellious Qi, relieves acute conditions and stops pain; expels Wind-Dampness and benefits the knee and breast.
E 34.locp: On the anterolateral thigh, between the vastus lateralis and the lateral border of the rectus femoris tendon, 2 cun above the base of the patella.
E 34.ind: acute stomach pain; acid regurgitation; vomiting; mastitis, breast pain; knee pain and swelling; difficulty bending or straightening the knee; cold and pain of the leg; diarrhea

E 35.loc: Knee bent, in the hollow below the kneecap, on the outer side of the kneecap tendon.
E 35.act: Soothes the knee, expels local Cold and Dampness.
E 35.fn: Expels Wind, Cold and Dampness, reduces swelling, relieves pain and benefits the knee.
E 35.locp: On the anterior knee, with the knee flexed, in the depression lateral to the patellar ligament (the lateral eye of the knee).
E 35.ind: knee pain; swelling of the knee; stiffness, difficulty bending or straightening the knee; knee osteoarthritis; weakness and numbness of the leg; weak, swollen legs (beriberi)
E 35.ci: Needle with the knee flexed, directed posteromedially, under strict asepsis (close to the joint cavity). Moxibustion is prohibited in the classical lists, but warm needling is commonly used here today.

E 36.loc: 3 cun below ST 35 (outer hollow of the knee), 1 finger-width outside the crest of the shinbone.
E 36.act: Tonifies the Qi and Blood of the Spleen and Stomach, strengthens the whole body.
E 36.fn: Harmonizes the Stomach and strengthens the Spleen, resolves Dampness; tonifies Qi and Blood and supports the upright Qi (Zheng Qi); raises Yang, strengthens the defensive Qi, calms the Shen; regulates the intestines and frees the channel.
E 36.locp: On the anterior leg, on the line from ST 35 to ST 41, 3 cun below ST 35, one finger-width (middle finger) lateral to the anterior crest of the tibia.
E 36.ind: stomach pain; nausea and vomiting; abdominal distension; diarrhea or constipation; poor appetite, slow digestion; fatigue and general weakness; dizziness; shortness of breath; insomnia, agitation; mastitis; edema; knee and leg pain and weakness
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Stomach
Lower He-Sea point of the Stomach
Point of the Sea of Water and Grain

E 37.loc: 3 cun below ST 36, 1 finger-width outside the crest of the shinbone.
E 37.act: Lower He-Sea point of the Large Intestine: regulates the bowels, eliminates Damp-Heat.
E 37.fn: Regulates the intestines, Spleen and Stomach, clears Damp-Heat and resolves stagnation; expels Wind-Dampness and frees the channel.
E 37.locp: On the anterior leg, on the line from ST 35 to ST 41, 6 cun below ST 35 (3 cun below ST 36), one finger-width lateral to the anterior crest of the tibia.
E 37.ind: diarrhea; dysentery; abdominal pain; borborygmus; constipation; appendicitis pain; undigested food in the stool; weakness and paralysis of the leg; knee pain; weak, swollen legs (beriberi)
cats: Lower He-Sea point of the Large Intestine
Point of the Sea of Blood (Chong Mai)

E 38.loc: On the anterior leg, on the line from ST 35 to ST 41, 8 cun below ST 35 (halfway down the leg), one finger-width lateral to the anterior crest of the tibia.
E 38.act: Frees the channel and collaterals, expels Wind-Dampness; benefits the shoulder (empirical use).
E 38.ind: frozen shoulder, shoulder pain and stiffness; numbness and cold of the leg; weakness and wasting of the lower limbs; knee pain and swelling; calf cramps; abdominal pain
E 38.ci: Moxibustion is classically prohibited at this point (traditional list of points forbidden to moxibustion).

E 39.loc: On the anterior leg, on the line from ST 35 to ST 41, 9 cun below ST 35 (1 cun below ST 38), one finger-width lateral to the anterior crest of the tibia.
E 39.act: Regulates the Small Intestine and bowels, moves Qi, clears Damp-Heat; expels Wind-Dampness and frees the channel.
E 39.ind: lower abdominal pain radiating to the lower back or testicles; diarrhea with undigested food; dysentery, blood in the stool; scanty, dark urine; mastitis; weakness and paralysis of the leg; foot pain
cats: Lower He-Sea point of the Small Intestine
Point of the Sea of Blood (Chong Mai)

E 40.loc: On the leg, halfway between the knee and the outer ankle bone, 2 finger-widths outside the crest of the shinbone.
E 40.act: Major point for Phlegm (Tan): transforms it wherever it lodges (lungs, throat, neck, thyroid, lymph nodes), and Dampness too; calms the mind.
E 40.fn: Transforms Phlegm and Dampness, descends Lung and Stomach Qi, unbinds the chest; calms the Shen and frees the channel.
E 40.locp: On the anterolateral leg, at the lateral border of the tibialis anterior, 8 cun above the prominence of the lateral malleolus (one finger-width lateral to ST 38).
E 40.ind: cough with copious sputum; asthma; chest oppression; dizziness and headache from Phlegm; nausea; sensation of a lump in the throat; mania, epilepsy; constipation; heaviness of the body; pain, weakness or wasting of the leg; goiter, nodules and lymph nodes from Phlegm

E 41.loc: On the anterior ankle, in the depression at the center of the front of the ankle joint, between the tendons of extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum longus.
E 41.act: Clears Heat from the Stomach channel, calms the Shen, frees the channel and benefits the ankle.
E 41.ind: ankle pain and weakness; ankle sprain; foot drop; frontal headache; dizziness; red eyes; agitation, mental disorders; constipation and abdominal distension; swollen face

E 42.loc: On the top of the foot, at the joint between the base of the 2nd metatarsal and the intermediate cuneiform bone, over the dorsalis pedis artery (highest point of the instep).
E 42.act: Tonifies the Stomach and Spleen, harmonizes the Stomach, calms the Shen and frees the channel.
E 42.ind: stomach pain and distension; poor appetite; facial paralysis, deviated mouth; toothache; swollen face; mania; pain and swelling of the top of the foot; weakness and wasting of the foot
E 42.ci: Needle while avoiding the dorsalis pedis artery.

E 43.loc: On the top of the foot, between the 2nd and 3rd metatarsals, in the depression just proximal to the 2nd metatarsophalangeal joint.
E 43.act: Regulates the Spleen and resolves edema, harmonizes the Stomach and intestines, frees the channel.
E 43.ind: swelling of the face; swelling of the feet; abdominal pain; borborygmus; red, painful eyes; fever; pain and swelling of the top of the foot

E 44.loc: Top of the foot, between the 2nd and 3rd toes, at the edge of the web.
E 44.act: Clears Stomach Heat, soothes the gums and face.
E 44.fn: Clears Heat from the Stomach channel and Yang Ming, eliminates Damp-Heat from the intestines, calms the Shen and relieves pain.
E 44.locp: On the top of the foot, between the 2nd and 3rd toes, proximal to the web margin, at the border between the dorsal and plantar skin.
E 44.ind: toothache, swollen gums; bleeding gums; nosebleed; sore throat; facial paralysis; burning stomach pain; diarrhea, dysentery; constipation; fever; pain and swelling of the top of the foot

E 45.loc: On the 2nd toe, lateral side of the distal phalanx, 0.1 cun from the lateral corner of the nail.
E 45.act: Clears Heat from the Stomach channel, calms the Shen and settles sleep, restores consciousness.
E 45.ind: excessive dreaming, nightmares; insomnia; agitation, mania; nosebleed; toothache; sore throat; facial paralysis; fever; fainting; cold foot and leg

Rt 1.loc: At the inner corner of the big toenail, 0.1 cun from the corner of the nail.
Rt 1.act: Helps the Spleen hold the Blood, calms the mind.
Rt 1.fn: Strengthens the Spleen so that it holds the Blood in the vessels and stops bleeding (especially with moxa), calms the Shen and restores consciousness.
Rt 1.locp: On the medial side of the big toe, 0.1 cun proximal and medial to the medial corner of the toenail, where lines along the medial border and the base of the nail meet.
Rt 1.ind: uterine bleeding, heavy periods; blood in the stools or urine; nosebleed; abdominal distension; vomiting, diarrhea; excessive dreaming, insomnia; restlessness, sadness; loss of consciousness; childhood convulsions
cats: One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

Rt 2.loc: On the medial side of the big toe, in the depression distal to the first metatarsophalangeal joint, at the junction of the red and white skin (border between dorsal and plantar skin).
Rt 2.act: Strengthens the Spleen and harmonizes the Middle Energizer, clears Heat and promotes sweating in febrile diseases.
Rt 2.ind: abdominal distension and fullness; epigastric pain; vomiting; diarrhea or constipation; febrile disease without sweating; cold hands and feet; heaviness of the body; restlessness, insomnia; pain and swelling of the big toe

Rt 3.loc: Inner edge of the foot, in the hollow behind and below the head of the 1st metatarsal (just past the bump at the base of the big toe).
Rt 3.act: Yuan-Source point of the Spleen: tonifies the Spleen, transforms Dampness.
Rt 3.fn: Tonifies Spleen Qi and Spleen Yang, resolves Dampness and Damp-Heat, harmonizes the Spleen and Stomach, strengthens the spine.
Rt 3.locp: On the medial side of the foot, in the depression proximal and inferior to the head of the first metatarsal bone (just behind the big toe joint), at the junction of the red and white skin.
Rt 3.ind: fatigue, heaviness of the body; poor appetite; abdominal distension and pain; loose stools, diarrhea with undigested food; borborygmus; nausea, vomiting; constipation; heavy, painful joints; chronic low back pain; pain and swelling of the foot
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Spleen

Rt 4.loc: Inner edge of the foot, in the hollow in front of and below the base of the 1st metatarsal.
Rt 4.act: Harmonizes the Spleen and Stomach, eases belly pain.
Rt 4.fn: Strengthens the Spleen and Stomach, regulates the Penetrating Vessel and menstruation, subdues rebellious Qi, stops abdominal pain and calms the Shen.
Rt 4.locp: On the medial side of the foot, in the depression anterior and inferior to the base of the first metatarsal bone, at the junction of the red and white skin (about 1 cun proximal to SP 3).
Rt 4.ind: epigastric pain; nausea, vomiting; abdominal distension; borborygmus, diarrhea; dysentery; irregular or painful periods; uterine bleeding; chest oppression and pain; palpitations; restlessness, insomnia; facial edema
cats: Opening (confluent) point of the Chong Mai, paired with PC 6

Rt 5.loc: Anterior and inferior to the medial malleolus, in the depression midway between the tuberosity of the navicular bone and the prominence of the medial malleolus.
Rt 5.act: Strengthens the Spleen and Stomach, resolves Dampness, calms the Shen, relaxes the tendons and benefits the ankle.
Rt 5.ind: abdominal distension, borborygmus; loose stools, diarrhea; poor appetite; heaviness of the body; jaundice; hemorrhoids; stiffness and pain at the root of the tongue; excessive dreaming, sighing; pain and swelling of the ankle; pain of the inner thigh

Rt 6.loc: 3 cun above the tip of the inner ankle bone, just behind the edge of the shinbone.
Rt 6.act: Meeting point of the three Yin channels of the leg: tonifies the Spleen, nourishes Blood and Yin, calms the mind.
Rt 6.fn: Tonifies the Spleen and Stomach, resolves Dampness, regulates the Liver and tonifies the Kidney; nourishes Blood and Yin, moves Blood, regulates menstruation and the Lower Energizer, calms the Shen.
Rt 6.locp: On the medial side of the leg, 3 cun above the prominence of the medial malleolus, just posterior to the medial border of the tibia.
Rt 6.ind: irregular, painful or absent periods; uterine bleeding; infertility; difficult labor, retained placenta; vaginal discharge; difficult urination, enuresis; impotence, seminal emission; abdominal distension, loose stools with undigested food; insomnia, palpitations; dizziness; eczema, urticaria; pain and edema of the legs
Rt 6.ci: Contraindicated during pregnancy: it moves Blood downward and may promote contractions (classically combined with LI 4 to hasten labor).
cats: Meeting point of the three leg Yin (Spleen, Liver, Kidney)

Rt 7.loc: On the medial side of the leg, 6 cun above the prominence of the medial malleolus (3 cun above SP 6), just posterior to the medial border of the tibia.
Rt 7.act: Strengthens the Spleen, drains Dampness and promotes urination, activates the channel.
Rt 7.ind: abdominal distension; borborygmus; poor appetite, weight loss despite eating enough; difficult urination; edema of the legs; seminal emission; cold and numbness of the knee and leg; swelling and pain of the ankle

Rt 8.loc: 3 cun below SP 9, just behind the inner edge of the shinbone.
Rt 8.act: Xi-Cleft point of the Spleen: moves the Blood, eases painful periods.
Rt 8.fn: Regulates the Spleen and resolves Dampness, moves Blood and dispels Blood Stasis in the uterus, regulates menstruation and stops acute pain.
Rt 8.locp: On the medial side of the leg, 3 cun below SP 9, just posterior to the medial border of the tibia, on the line joining SP 9 to the medial malleolus.
Rt 8.ind: painful periods, especially acute attacks; irregular periods; abdominal masses in women; uterine bleeding; abdominal distension, loss of appetite; diarrhea; difficult urination, edema; seminal emission; low back pain; leg pain

Rt 9.loc: Inner side of the leg, in the hollow below the top of the shinbone (below the inner bump of the knee).
Rt 9.act: Drains Dampness, especially from the lower body.
Rt 9.fn: Regulates the Spleen and resolves Dampness, drains Dampness and Damp-Heat from the Lower Energizer, opens the water passages and promotes urination, benefits the knee.
Rt 9.locp: On the medial side of the leg, in the depression between the inferior border of the medial condyle of the tibia and the medial border of the tibia: sliding a finger up the tibial border, it stops beneath the condyle.
Rt 9.ind: edema, especially of the legs; urinary retention or difficult urination; burning urination, cloudy urine; enuresis, incontinence; diarrhea, dysentery; abdominal distension; jaundice; vaginal discharge; genital pain; low back pain; pain and swelling of the knee

Rt 10.loc: Knee bent, 2 cun above the upper inner corner of the kneecap, on the bulge of the muscle.
Rt 10.act: “Sea of Blood”: moves and cools the Blood, soothes the skin.
Rt 10.fn: Moves Blood and dispels Blood Stasis, cools the Blood, regulates menstruation and harmonizes the Blood to benefit the skin.
Rt 10.locp: On the anteromedial thigh, with the knee flexed, 2 cun above the medial end of the base of the patella, on the bulge of the vastus medialis muscle.
Rt 10.ind: irregular or painful periods; amenorrhea; uterine bleeding from Heat in the Blood; eczema; urticaria; itching, especially genital; boils, hot sores; burning urination; pain of the inner thigh; knee pain
Rt 10.ci: Use with caution during pregnancy: the point strongly moves Blood.

Rt 11.loc: On the medial thigh, at the junction of the upper third and lower two thirds of the line from the medial end of the base of the patella to SP 12, between the sartorius and adductor longus muscles, over the femoral artery (WHO 2008; older Chinese texts place it 6 cun above SP 10).
Rt 11.act: Drains Dampness and promotes urination, clears Damp-Heat from the Lower Energizer.
Rt 11.ind: urinary retention; painful, difficult urination; enuresis; damp itching of the genitals; swelling and pain of the groin; pain and weakness of the thigh
Rt 11.ci: Lies over the femoral artery: palpate the pulse and needle beside it, shallowly. Listed among the points forbidden to needling in the Zhen Jiu Da Cheng.

Rt 12.loc: In the groin, on the inguinal crease, just lateral to the pulsating femoral artery, about 3.5 cun lateral to the midline at the level of the upper border of the pubic symphysis.
Rt 12.act: Moves Qi and Blood in the lower abdomen and stops pain, drains Dampness and clears Heat, promotes urination.
Rt 12.ind: lower abdominal pain; inguinal hernia; abdominal masses; urinary retention or difficult urination; vaginal discharge; uterine bleeding; hemorrhoids; pain and weakness of the leg
Rt 12.ci: Avoid the femoral artery (palpate the pulse and needle lateral to it). Not advised during pregnancy (lower abdomen).

Rt 13.loc: On the lower abdomen, 4.3 cun below the centre of the umbilicus and 4 cun lateral to the anterior midline (0.7 cun above SP 12).
Rt 13.act: Moves Qi, dispels Stagnation and accumulations in the lower abdomen, stops pain.
Rt 13.ind: lower abdominal pain; hernia; abdominal masses; abdominal distension; constipation; pain of the hip and thigh
Rt 13.ci: Not advised in late pregnancy. Avoid deep needling in thin patients (abdominal cavity).

Rt 14.loc: On the abdomen, 1.3 cun below the centre of the umbilicus and 4 cun lateral to the anterior midline, directly below SP 15.
Rt 14.act: Warms and regulates the Middle Energizer, moves the Qi of the intestines, subdues rebellious Qi.
Rt 14.ind: pain around the umbilicus; abdominal pain from Cold; diarrhea; dysentery; constipation; abdominal distension; hernia
Rt 14.ci: Not advised in late pregnancy. Avoid deep needling in thin patients (abdominal cavity).

Rt 15.loc: On the abdomen, level with the centre of the umbilicus, 4 cun lateral to the anterior midline (on the mammillary line).
Rt 15.act: Regulates Qi and moves the intestines, strengthens the Spleen and the four limbs, resolves Dampness.
Rt 15.ind: constipation; loose stools, diarrhea; dysentery; abdominal distension and pain; abdominal pain from Cold; weakness of the four limbs; sadness, frequent sighing
Rt 15.ci: Not advised in late pregnancy. Avoid deep needling in thin patients (abdominal cavity).

Rt 16.loc: On the upper abdomen, 3 cun above the centre of the umbilicus and 4 cun lateral to the anterior midline (level with CV 11).
Rt 16.act: Harmonizes the Spleen and intestines, aids digestion, stops abdominal pain.
Rt 16.ind: abdominal pain; pain around the umbilicus; indigestion; undigested food in the stools; constipation; dysentery with blood or pus
Rt 16.ci: Avoid deep needling in thin patients (abdominal cavity; liver on the right side).

Rt 17.loc: On the chest, in the fifth intercostal space, 6 cun lateral to the anterior midline (2 cun lateral to the mammillary line).
Rt 17.act: Strengthens the Spleen and promotes the movement of fluids, opens the chest and ribs, descends Stomach Qi.
Rt 17.ind: fullness and pain of the chest and ribs; abdominal distension; vomiting right after eating; regurgitation; borborygmus; edema, ascites
Rt 17.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely or transversely along the intercostal space, never deeply.

Rt 18.loc: On the chest, in the fourth intercostal space, 6 cun lateral to the anterior midline (2 cun lateral to the nipple).
Rt 18.act: Opens the chest, descends Lung Qi and calms cough, promotes lactation and benefits the breast.
Rt 18.ind: chest oppression and pain; cough; hiccups; insufficient lactation; breast abscess, mastitis; rib pain
Rt 18.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely or transversely along the intercostal space, never deeply.

Rt 19.loc: On the chest, in the third intercostal space, 6 cun lateral to the anterior midline.
Rt 19.act: Regulates Qi in the chest and ribs, stops pain.
Rt 19.ind: fullness and pain of the chest and ribs; chest pain radiating to the back; inability to lie down or turn over because of pain; chest oppression; cough; shortness of breath
Rt 19.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely or transversely along the intercostal space, never deeply.

Rt 20.loc: On the chest, in the second intercostal space, 6 cun lateral to the anterior midline.
Rt 20.act: Descends Lung Qi, opens the chest, resolves Phlegm.
Rt 20.ind: cough; thick or purulent sputum; shortness of breath; fullness and oppression of the chest; rib pain; difficulty swallowing, poor appetite
Rt 20.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely or transversely along the intercostal space, never deeply.

Rt 21.loc: On the lateral chest, in the sixth intercostal space, on the midaxillary line (about 6 cun below the axilla).
Rt 21.act: Moves Qi and Blood in the Luo vessels throughout the body, opens the chest and ribs, relieves widespread pain and weakness of the limbs.
Rt 21.ind: widespread pain throughout the body; slackness and weakness of the joints and four limbs; pain and fullness of the ribs; chest pain; shortness of breath, dyspnea; cough; marked fatigue
Rt 21.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely or transversely along the intercostal space, never deeply.

C 1.loc: At the centre of the axillary fossa, with the arm abducted, over the axillary artery (palpable pulse).
C 1.act: Opens the chest and moves Heart Qi, activates the channel to benefit the shoulder and arm.
C 1.ind: heart pain, chest pain; palpitations; chest oppression, shortness of breath; rib pain; sadness, anxiety; dry throat with thirst; frozen shoulder, inability to raise the arm; numbness or coldness of the arm; excessive underarm sweating; swollen axillary lymph nodes
C 1.ci: Avoid the axillary artery (palpate the pulse and needle beside it); shallow insertion without strong manipulation.

C 2.loc: On the medial side of the arm, 3 cun above the cubital crease, just medial to the biceps brachii muscle (medial bicipital groove).
C 2.act: Activates the channel and stops pain, benefits the shoulder and arm.
C 2.ind: pain and swelling of the shoulder and arm; inability to raise the shoulder and arm; armpit pain; rib pain; headache with chills; yellow eyes
C 2.ci: Classically forbidden to needling (moxa was preferred); if needled, avoid the brachial artery and median nerve.

C 3.loc: With the elbow flexed, on the anteromedial side of the elbow, just anterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus, level with the cubital crease (midway between the medial end of the crease and the epicondyle).
C 3.act: Calms the Shen, clears Heat and Fire, resolves Phlegm, activates the channel at the elbow and arm.
C 3.ind: heart pain; agitation, mental disorders, epilepsy; poor memory; dizziness; swollen lymph nodes of the neck and armpit; tremor of the hand and arm; pain and contracture of the elbow; numbness of the arm; toothache; rib pain

C 4.loc: On the anterior forearm, 1.5 cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease, on the radial side of the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon.
C 4.act: Calms the Shen, benefits the voice, relaxes the tendons of the arm.
C 4.ind: sudden loss of voice; heart pain; palpitations; sadness, fear; pain and contracture of the elbow and arm; numbness and pain of the wrist
C 4.ci: Needle on the radial side of the tendon, avoiding the ulnar artery and nerve.

C 5.loc: Inner side of the wrist, 1 cun above the crease, on the little-finger side, against the tendon.
C 5.act: Tonifies Heart Qi, calms the mind.
C 5.fn: Calms the Shen, regulates the Heart rhythm, benefits the tongue and speech, benefits the Bladder.
C 5.locp: On the anterior forearm, 1 cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease, on the radial side of the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon.
C 5.ind: palpitations; fear, anxiety; sudden loss of voice; stiff tongue, difficulty speaking after a stroke; insomnia; dizziness, headache; enuresis; pain of the wrist and elbow
C 5.ci: Needle on the radial side of the tendon, avoiding the ulnar artery and nerve.

C 6.loc: Inner side of the wrist, 0.5 cun above the crease, on the little-finger side, against the tendon.
C 6.act: Xi-Cleft point of the Heart: nourishes Heart Yin, stops night sweats.
C 6.fn: Nourishes Heart Yin and clears Deficiency Heat, stops night sweats and bleeding, calms the Shen and acute heart pain.
C 6.locp: On the anterior forearm, 0.5 cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease, on the radial side of the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon.
C 6.ind: night sweats; palpitations, fear; acute heart pain; restlessness, insomnia; hot flushes, hot palms; nosebleed; coughing or vomiting blood; sudden loss of voice
C 6.ci: Needle on the radial side of the tendon, avoiding the ulnar artery and nerve.

C 7.loc: In the wrist crease on the little-finger side, in the hollow against the tendon.
C 7.act: Yuan-Source point of the Heart: calms the mind, helps sleep and memory.
C 7.fn: Calms the Shen, nourishes Heart Blood, tonifies the Heart and clears Heart Heat.
C 7.locp: On the palmar wrist crease, on the radial side of the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon, just at the proximal border of the pisiform bone.
C 7.ind: insomnia, excessive dreaming; anxiety, fear; palpitations; poor memory; agitation, mental disorders; sadness, depression; epilepsy; heart pain; dry mouth and throat; wrist pain
C 7.ci: Needle on the radial side of the tendon, avoiding the ulnar artery and nerve.

C 8.loc: In the palm, between the 4th and 5th metacarpals, where the tip of your little finger lands when you make a fist.
C 8.fn: Clears Fire from the Heart and Small Intestine, calms the Shen, regulates Heart Qi.
C 8.locp: On the palm, between the fourth and fifth metacarpal bones, proximal to the fifth metacarpophalangeal joint, where the tip of the little finger rests when making a fist (level with PC 8).
C 8.ind: palpitations; agitation, anxiety; heart pain; hot palms; ulcers of the mouth and tongue; burning urination, dark urine; urinary retention, enuresis; genital itching and pain; contracture of the little finger
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Heart

C 9.loc: On the radial side of the little finger, 0.1 cun proximal and lateral to the radial corner of the nail.
C 9.act: Clears Heat and Fire from the Heart, opens the orifices and restores consciousness, extinguishes Wind and calms the Shen.
C 9.ind: loss of consciousness, stroke; high fever; heart pain; palpitations; agitation, mental disorders; pain of the chest and ribs; sore throat, swollen tongue; red, painful eyes; hot palms; convulsions

IG 1.loc: On the ulnar side of the little finger, 0.1 cun proximal and medial to the ulnar corner of the nail.
IG 1.act: Promotes lactation and benefits the breast, clears Heat, opens the orifices and restores consciousness.
IG 1.ind: insufficient lactation; breast abscess, mastitis; loss of consciousness, stroke; febrile disease; sore throat; tinnitus, deafness; headache; corneal opacity; nosebleed; neck pain

IG 2.loc: On the ulnar side of the hand, in the depression distal to the fifth metacarpophalangeal joint, at the junction of the red and white skin (end of the flexion crease with a loose fist).
IG 2.act: Clears Heat and Wind-Heat, reduces swelling, benefits the eyes, ears and throat, promotes lactation.
IG 2.ind: febrile disease without sweating; sore throat, mumps; tinnitus; red, painful eyes; nosebleed; insufficient lactation; dark urine; stiffness and pain of the neck; numbness of the fingers; arm pain

IG 3.loc: On the ulnar side of the hand, in the depression proximal to the fifth metacarpophalangeal joint, at the junction of the red and white skin; with a loose fist, at the end of the distal palmar crease.
IG 3.act: Opens the Governing Vessel and relaxes the neck and back, relaxes the tendons, expels Wind and clears Heat, calms the Shen, treats malaria.
IG 3.ind: neck stiffness and pain, torticollis; acute low back sprain; pain of the shoulder and elbow; contracture of the fingers; occipital headache; tinnitus, deafness; red, painful eyes; fever and chills, malaria; night sweats; epilepsy, mental disorders
cats: Tonification point of the Small Intestine
Opening (confluent) point of the Du Mai (Governing Vessel), paired with BL 62

IG 4.loc: On the ulnar side of the wrist, in the depression between the base of the fifth metacarpal bone and the triquetrum, at the junction of the red and white skin.
IG 4.act: Clears Damp-Heat and relieves jaundice, expels Wind, benefits the neck, activates the channel.
IG 4.ind: jaundice; rib pain; intense thirst (diabetes); febrile disease without sweating; headache; tinnitus; tearing, corneal opacity; neck stiffness; pain of the wrist, elbow and fingers
cats: Yuan-Source point of the Small Intestine

IG 5.loc: On the ulnar side of the wrist, in the depression between the triquetrum and the styloid process of the ulna, level with the dorsal wrist crease.
IG 5.act: Clears Heat and reduces swelling, calms the Shen, benefits the wrist.
IG 5.ind: febrile disease; swelling of the neck and jaw; toothache; tinnitus, deafness; dizziness; agitation, incoherent speech; neck pain; pain of the arm and side of the body; wrist pain
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Small Intestine

IG 6.loc: On the dorsal forearm, ulnar side, 1 cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease, in the depression on the radial side of the head of the ulna; the depression appears when the palm is turned toward the chest.
IG 6.act: Brightens the eyes, relaxes the tendons, activates the channel and stops acute pain.
IG 6.ind: declining eyesight, blurred vision; pain of the shoulder and arm "as if broken"; neck stiffness, torticollis; acute low back sprain; difficulty sitting down and standing up; pain and stiffness of the wrist
cats: Xi-Cleft point of the Small Intestine

IG 7.loc: On the posteromedial forearm, 5 cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease, on the line from SI 5 to SI 8, between the medial border of the ulna and the flexor carpi ulnaris muscle.
IG 7.act: Clears Heat, releases the exterior, calms the Shen, activates the channel.
IG 7.ind: fever with chills; neck stiffness; headache, dizziness; anxiety, fear; agitation, mental disorders; pain and contracture of the elbow; finger pain; warts
cats: Luo-Connecting point of the Small Intestine

IG 8.loc: On the posteromedial elbow, with the elbow flexed, in the depression between the olecranon and the medial epicondyle of the humerus (ulnar nerve groove).
IG 8.act: Clears Heat and reduces swelling, calms the Shen, activates the channel and benefits the elbow.
IG 8.ind: elbow pain; pain of the shoulder and back of the arm; numbness of the ring and little fingers; swollen cheeks; toothache; neck pain; epilepsy; swollen lymph nodes of the neck; deafness
IG 8.ci: The ulnar nerve lies beneath the point: needle shallowly and stop if an electric sensation occurs.
cats: Sedation point of the Small Intestine

IG 9.loc: On the posterior shoulder, posteroinferior to the shoulder joint, 1 cun above the end of the posterior axillary fold, with the arm by the side.
IG 9.act: Expels Wind, activates the channel and benefits the shoulder.
IG 9.ind: pain of the shoulder and scapula; frozen shoulder; inability to raise the arm; numbness or paralysis of the arm; tinnitus, deafness; swollen lymph nodes of the neck and armpit
IG 9.ci: Needle perpendicularly, never medially toward the thorax (risk of pneumothorax).

IG 10.loc: On the posterior shoulder, directly above the posterior axillary fold, in the depression below the inferior border of the spine of the scapula.
IG 10.act: Activates the channel, benefits the shoulder and reduces swelling.
IG 10.ind: pain and swelling of the shoulder; shoulder pain radiating to the scapula; weakness of the shoulder and arm; inability to raise the arm; frozen shoulder; swollen lymph nodes of the neck

IG 11.loc: On the scapula, in the infraspinous fossa, in the depression at the junction of the upper third and lower two thirds of the line from the midpoint of the scapular spine to the inferior angle of the scapula; often tender on pressure.
IG 11.act: Activates the channel and benefits the scapula, moves Qi in the chest and ribs, benefits the breast.
IG 11.ind: scapular pain; pain of the shoulder and back of the arm; inability to raise the arm; elbow pain; fullness and pain of the chest and ribs; breast abscess, mastitis; breast pain, insufficient lactation; cough

IG 12.loc: On the scapula, at the centre of the supraspinous fossa, just above the midpoint of the scapular spine (directly above SI 11); a depression appears when the arm is raised.
IG 12.act: Expels Wind, activates the channel, benefits the shoulder and scapula.
IG 12.ind: pain of the shoulder and scapula; inability to raise the arm; numbness and pain of the arm; neck stiffness; inability to turn the head; contracture of the upper limb
IG 12.ci: Do not needle deeply forward or medially (risk of pneumothorax).

IG 13.loc: On the scapula, in the depression above the medial end of the spine of the scapula (medial end of the supraspinous fossa).
IG 13.act: Activates the channel, relaxes the tendons, benefits the shoulder and scapula.
IG 13.ind: pain and stiffness of the scapula; contracture of the shoulder; upper back pain; shoulder pain radiating into the arm; numbness of the upper limb; neck stiffness
IG 13.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely, never deeply and perpendicularly, especially in thin patients.

IG 14.loc: On the upper back, level with the inferior border of the spinous process of the first thoracic vertebra (T1), 3 cun lateral to the posterior midline (in line with the medial border of the scapula).
IG 14.act: Expels Wind and Cold, relaxes the tendons, activates the channel, benefits the shoulder and neck.
IG 14.ind: pain of the shoulder and upper back; stiffness and pain of the neck; torticollis; coldness and pain of the scapula; numbness of the arm; contracture of the shoulder
IG 14.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely, never deeply and perpendicularly, especially in thin patients.

IG 15.loc: On the upper back, level with the inferior border of the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra (C7), 2 cun lateral to the posterior midline.
IG 15.act: Descends Lung Qi and calms cough, activates the channel, benefits the shoulder and back.
IG 15.ind: cough; asthma, shortness of breath; coughing blood; fever and chills; pain of the shoulder and upper back; neck stiffness; blurred vision
IG 15.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely, never deeply and perpendicularly, especially in thin patients.

IG 16.loc: On the lateral neck, level with the upper border of the thyroid cartilage (Adam's apple), just posterior to the posterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
IG 16.act: Benefits the ears and throat, calms the Shen, descends Qi, activates the channel in the neck.
IG 16.ind: deafness, tinnitus; pain and swelling of the throat; sudden loss of voice; goiter; swollen cheeks; stiffness and pain of the neck; shoulder pain; agitation, mental disorders
IG 16.ci: Shallow insertion only, avoiding the carotid artery and jugular vein.

IG 17.loc: On the lateral neck, posterior to the angle of the mandible, in the depression anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
IG 17.act: Benefits the throat and neck, subdues rebellious Qi, reduces swelling and dissipates nodules.
IG 17.ind: sore throat; sensation of a lump in the throat; swelling of the neck and cheeks; goiter; swollen lymph nodes of the neck; tinnitus, deafness; difficulty speaking; cough, chest oppression; stiff neck, inability to turn the head
IG 17.ci: Needle toward the root of the tongue without excessive depth, avoiding the carotid artery and internal jugular vein.

IG 18.loc: On the face, below the cheekbone (inferior border of the zygomatic bone), in the depression directly below the outer canthus of the eye.
IG 18.act: Expels Wind, clears Heat, reduces swelling and stops facial pain.
IG 18.ind: facial paralysis; twitching of the eyelids and face; facial (trigeminal) neuralgia; toothache; swollen cheeks; red face; yellow eyes
IG 18.ci: Moxa classically forbidden (face, close to the eye).

IG 19.loc: In front of the ear, in the hollow that forms when you open your mouth.
IG 19.act: Soothes the ears: ringing in the ears (tinnitus), blocked ear.
IG 19.fn: Benefits the ears and hearing, calms the Shen.
IG 19.locp: In front of the ear, in the depression between the anterior border of the tragus and the posterior border of the condylar process of the mandible, which appears when the mouth is open.
IG 19.ind: tinnitus; deafness; ear discharge, otitis; itching or pain of the ear; pain and locking of the jaw; toothache; loss of voice; epilepsy, mental disorders
IG 19.ci: Locate and needle with the mouth open; the mouth may be closed once the needle is in place.

V 1.loc: On the face, in the small depression just above and medial to the inner canthus of the eye, against the medial wall of the orbit (about 0.1 cun superomedial to the inner canthus).
V 1.act: Expels Wind and clears Heat, brightens the eyes; a major point for eye disorders, whether of external origin (Wind-Heat) or from internal Deficiency (Liver, Kidney).
V 1.ind: red, swollen and painful eyes; tearing in the wind; itchy eyes; blurred vision; night blindness; color blindness; nearsightedness; early cataract; pterygium; acute low back pain
V 1.ci: Moxibustion is contraindicated. Needling for trained practitioners only: gently push the eyeball aside, insert slowly along the orbital wall without lifting, thrusting or rotating, and press for a few minutes after withdrawal to prevent a hematoma.

V 2.loc: In the small hollow at the inner end of the eyebrow.
V 2.act: Soothes the eyes and headaches in the forehead.
V 2.fn: Expels Wind, clears Heat, brightens the eyes and relieves pain; frees the channels of the forehead and calms eyelid spasms.
V 2.locp: On the face, in the depression at the medial end of the eyebrow, over the frontal notch (a small palpable notch on the orbital rim), directly above the inner canthus.
V 2.ind: frontal headache; pain of the eyebrow and orbit; red, painful eyes; tearing; blurred vision; twitching eyelids; drooping eyelid; facial paralysis; sinusitis and blocked nose; hiccups
V 2.ci: Moxibustion is contraindicated (close to the eye, classical list). Needle transversely under the skin, downward or along the eyebrow, without going deep toward the orbit.

V 3.loc: On the head, directly above the medial end of the eyebrow (BL 2), 0.5 cun above the anterior hairline, between GV 24 and BL 4.
V 3.act: Expels Wind, clears the head and eyes, opens the nose.
V 3.ind: frontal headache; dizziness; blocked nose; loss of smell; sores inside the nose; blurred vision; epilepsy

V 4.loc: On the head, 0.5 cun above the anterior hairline and 1.5 cun lateral to the midline, at the junction of the medial and middle thirds of the line from GV 24 to ST 8.
V 4.act: Clears the head and brightens the eyes, opens the nose, expels Wind.
V 4.ind: frontal and vertex headache; blocked nose; nosebleeds; rhinitis; blurred vision; eye pain; dizziness

V 5.loc: On the head, 1 cun above the anterior hairline and 1.5 cun lateral to the midline, 0.5 cun behind BL 4.
V 5.act: Expels Wind, clears the head, subdues internal Wind and calms convulsions.
V 5.ind: headache; dizziness; blurred vision; epilepsy; convulsions in children; eyes rolling upward; arching stiffness of the neck and back

V 6.loc: On the head, 2.5 cun above the anterior hairline and 1.5 cun lateral to the midline, 1.5 cun behind BL 5.
V 6.act: Expels Wind, clears Heat from the head, brightens the eyes.
V 6.ind: headache; dizziness; blurred vision; eye pain; blocked nose with profuse discharge; colds with fever and no sweating; vomiting with restlessness
V 6.ci: Moxibustion is forbidden in the classical lists of points not to be moxibusted. Needle transversely under the scalp.

V 7.loc: On the head, 4 cun above the anterior hairline and 1.5 cun lateral to the midline (that is, 1 cun anterior and 1.5 cun lateral to GV 20).
V 7.act: Opens the nose, expels Wind, clears the head.
V 7.ind: blocked nose; loss of smell; rhinitis and sinusitis; nosebleeds; vertex headache; heavy head; dizziness; facial paralysis

V 8.loc: On the head, 5.5 cun above the anterior hairline and 1.5 cun lateral to the midline, 1.5 cun behind BL 7 (slightly behind the level of GV 20).
V 8.act: Clears the head and sense organs, brightens the eyes, calms the Shen (mind).
V 8.ind: dizziness; tinnitus; blurred vision; blocked nose; headache; mental agitation and mania; goiter
V 8.ci: Listed among the points forbidden to needling in classical texts: today it is only needled superficially and transversely, under the scalp.

V 9.loc: On the back of the head, level with the upper border of the external occipital protuberance (level with GV 17), 1.3 cun lateral to the midline.
V 9.act: Expels Wind and Cold, clears the head and eyes, relieves pain.
V 9.ind: occipital headache; heavy head; neck pain and stiffness; eye pain; blurred vision; blocked nose; dizziness; chilliness and aversion to cold
V 9.ci: Listed among the points forbidden to needling in classical texts: today it is only needled superficially and transversely.

V 10.loc: On the back of the neck, level with the upper border of the C2 spinous process, in the depression at the lateral border of the trapezius muscle, at the posterior hairline (about 1.3 cun lateral to the midline).
V 10.act: Expels Wind, clears the head and eyes, opens the sense orifices, relaxes the neck muscles and strengthens the back.
V 10.ind: occipital headache; stiff, painful neck; wry neck; dizziness; blurred vision and red eyes; blocked nose and loss of smell; sore throat; shoulder and back pain; low back pain; epilepsy
V 10.ci: Do not needle deeply upward and medially (medulla oblongata): needle perpendicularly or slightly laterally, 0.5 to 0.8 cun. Moxibustion is forbidden in the classical lists of points not to be moxibusted.

V 11.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 1st thoracic vertebra (T1), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 11.act: Strengthens the bones and joints, expels Wind and releases the exterior, helps Lung Qi descend.
V 11.ind: pain and stiffness of the bones and joints; pain and stiffness of the neck, shoulders and back; knee pain; colds with fever and chills; headache; cough; tightness in the chest
V 11.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely toward the spine (0.5 to 0.8 cun), never deeply and perpendicularly.
cats: Point of the Sea of Blood (Chong Mai)

V 12.loc: On the back, 1.5 cun on each side of the spine, below the 2nd thoracic vertebra.
V 12.act: “Wind Gate”: expels Wind, strengthens your defenses against colds.
V 12.fn: Expels Wind and releases the exterior, disperses and descends Lung Qi, strengthens the defensive (Wei) Qi.
V 12.locp: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 2nd thoracic vertebra (T2), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 12.ind: early-stage colds and flu; aversion to wind and cold; fever; headache; blocked or runny nose; cough; stiff neck; upper back pain; hives; frequent colds (moxibustion for prevention)
V 12.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely toward the spine (0.5 to 0.8 cun), never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 13.loc: On the back, 1.5 cun on each side of the spine, below the 3rd thoracic vertebra.
V 13.act: Back-Shu point of the Lung: tonifies Lung Qi.
V 13.fn: Tonifies Lung Qi and nourishes Lung Yin, regulates the dispersing and descending of the Lung, clears Lung Heat and calms cough and wheezing.
V 13.locp: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 3rd thoracic vertebra (T3), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline (roughly level with the medial end of the spine of the shoulder blade).
V 13.ind: acute or chronic cough; asthma; shortness of breath; tightness in the chest; coughing up blood; afternoon fever and night sweats; spontaneous sweating; blocked nose; itching and hives; sadness
V 13.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely toward the spine (0.5 to 0.8 cun), never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 14.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 4th thoracic vertebra (T4), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 14.act: Regulates the Heart and Pericardium, opens the chest, moves Qi and calms the Shen (mind).
V 14.ind: chest and heart pain; palpitations; tightness in the chest; cough; nausea and vomiting; anxiety and restlessness; upper back pain
V 14.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely toward the spine (0.5 to 0.8 cun), never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 15.loc: On the back, 1.5 cun on each side of the spine, below the 5th thoracic vertebra.
V 15.act: Back-Shu point of the Heart: tonifies the Heart, calms the mind.
V 15.fn: Tonifies and nourishes the Heart, calms the Shen (mind), clears Heart Fire, moves Heart Blood and opens the chest.
V 15.locp: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 5th thoracic vertebra (T5), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 15.ind: palpitations; insomnia and dream-disturbed sleep; anxiety; poor memory; chest pain; epilepsy and mental disorders; night sweats; nocturnal emissions; cough with blood
V 15.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely toward the spine (0.5 to 0.8 cun), never deeply and perpendicularly. Moxibustion is forbidden in the classical lists (sometimes used today, with care, for Heart Yang Deficiency).

V 16.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 6th thoracic vertebra (T6), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 16.act: Regulates Qi in the chest and abdomen, frees the Governing Vessel, relieves pain.
V 16.ind: chest and heart pain; palpitations; bloating and abdominal pain; borborygmi; hiccups; back pain; itchy skin
V 16.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely toward the spine (0.5 to 0.8 cun), never deeply and perpendicularly.
cats: Back-Shu point of the Governing Vessel

V 17.loc: On the back, 1.5 cun on each side of the spine, below the 7th thoracic vertebra, roughly level with the tips of the shoulder blades.
V 17.act: Meeting point of Blood: nourishes and moves the Blood.
V 17.fn: Moves Blood and dispels Blood Stasis, nourishes Blood, cools Blood and stops bleeding; relaxes the diaphragm and descends rebellious Qi.
V 17.locp: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 7th thoracic vertebra (T7), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline (roughly level with the lower tip of the shoulder blade).
V 17.ind: hiccups; vomiting; difficulty swallowing; fixed pain from Blood Stasis; anemia and Blood Deficiency; bleeding (nosebleed, coughing or vomiting blood, blood in the stools); night sweats; afternoon fever; cough and asthma; hives and itching
V 17.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely toward the spine (0.5 to 0.8 cun), never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 18.loc: On the back, 1.5 cun on each side of the spine, below the 9th thoracic vertebra.
V 18.act: Back-Shu point of the Liver: nourishes Liver Blood, soothes the eyes.
