V 18.fn: Spreads Liver Qi, nourishes Liver Blood, drains Damp-Heat from the Liver and Gallbladder, brightens the eyes and subdues internal Wind.
V 18.locp: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 9th thoracic vertebra (T9), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 18.ind: pain and distension under the ribs; jaundice; bitter taste; red, dry or painful eyes; blurred vision; night blindness; dizziness; irritability, anger, low mood; epilepsy; cramps and spasms; mid-back pain
V 18.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely toward the spine (0.5 to 0.8 cun), never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 19.loc: On the back, 1.5 cun on each side of the spine, below the 10th thoracic vertebra.
V 19.act: Back-Shu point of the Gallbladder: frees the Gallbladder, drains Damp-Heat, strengthens courage.
V 19.fn: Drains Damp-Heat from the Liver and Gallbladder, harmonizes the Stomach and relaxes the diaphragm, tonifies and regulates Gallbladder Qi.
V 19.locp: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 10th thoracic vertebra (T10), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 19.ind: pain under the ribs; jaundice; bitter taste in the mouth; nausea and vomiting; difficulty swallowing; dry mouth; afternoon fever with night sweats; timidity, fearfulness and indecision
V 19.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely toward the spine (0.5 to 0.8 cun), never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 20.loc: On the back, 1.5 cun on each side of the spine, below the 11th thoracic vertebra.
V 20.act: Back-Shu point of the Spleen: tonifies the Spleen, transforms Dampness.
V 20.fn: Tonifies the Spleen and Stomach, transforms Dampness, helps the Spleen hold the Blood, raises clear Qi and nourishes Blood.
V 20.locp: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 11th thoracic vertebra (T11), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 20.ind: bloating; poor appetite; loose stools or diarrhea; sluggish digestion; fatigue and heavy limbs; edema; jaundice; bleeding from Qi Deficiency (heavy periods, easy bruising, blood in the stools); organ prolapse; weight loss
V 20.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely toward the spine (0.5 to 0.8 cun), never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 21.loc: On the back, 1.5 cun on each side of the spine, below the 12th thoracic vertebra.
V 21.act: Back-Shu point of the Stomach: tonifies the Stomach.
V 21.fn: Harmonizes the Stomach and descends rebellious Qi, tonifies the Stomach and Spleen, transforms Dampness and resolves food stagnation.
V 21.locp: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 21.ind: epigastric pain and distension; nausea and vomiting; acid reflux; poor appetite or hunger without wanting to eat; sluggish digestion; borborygmi; diarrhea; weight loss; chest and back pain
V 21.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely toward the spine (0.5 to 0.8 cun), never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 22.loc: On the back, 1.5 cun on each side of the spine, below the 1st lumbar vertebra.
V 22.act: Back-Shu point of the Triple Energizer: opens the water passages, drains Dampness and swelling.
V 22.fn: Regulates the Triple Energizer, opens the water passages and promotes urination, transforms Dampness, strengthens the lower back.
V 22.locp: On the lower back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 1st lumbar vertebra (L1), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 22.ind: edema; difficult urination; scanty or cloudy urine; bloating; borborygmi; diarrhea with undigested food; vomiting; stiffness and pain of the lower back
V 22.ci: Do not needle too deeply (the kidney lies underneath): 0.8 to 1 cun perpendicularly.
cats: Back-Shu point of the Triple Energizer

V 23.loc: On the lower back, 1.5 cun on each side of the spine, below the 2nd lumbar vertebra, at waist level.
V 23.act: Back-Shu point of the Kidney: tonifies the Kidney, strengthens the lower back.
V 23.fn: Tonifies the Kidney and fortifies Essence (Jing), warms Kidney Yang and nourishes Kidney Yin, strengthens the lower back and bones; regulates the water passages, helps the Kidney grasp Qi and benefits the ears and eyes.
V 23.locp: On the lower back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 2nd lumbar vertebra (L2), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline (roughly at waist level).
V 23.ind: pain and weakness of the lower back; weak knees; frequent urination, bedwetting, incontinence; edema; impotence, seminal emissions, infertility; irregular periods and vaginal discharge; tinnitus and deafness; dizziness; chronic asthma; feeling cold and fatigue
V 23.ci: Do not needle too deeply (the kidney lies underneath): 0.8 to 1 cun perpendicularly.

V 24.loc: On the lower back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 3rd lumbar vertebra (L3), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 24.act: Strengthens the lower back and legs, regulates Qi and Blood in the lower body.
V 24.ind: low back pain; stiffness of the lower back; leg pain and weakness; painful periods; irregular periods; uterine bleeding between periods; hemorrhoids
cats: Back-Shu point of the Sea of Qi

V 25.loc: On the lower back, 1.5 cun on each side of the spine, below the 4th lumbar vertebra, level with the top of the pelvis.
V 25.act: Back-Shu point of the Large Intestine: regulates bowel movements, soothes the lower back.
V 25.fn: Regulates the intestines and bowel movements, moves Qi and resolves stagnation, strengthens the lower back and legs.
V 25.locp: On the lower back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 4th lumbar vertebra (L4), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline (level with the top of the iliac crests).
V 25.ind: constipation; diarrhea; bloating and borborygmi; pain around the navel; dysentery; low back pain and stiffness; sciatica; leg weakness
cats: Back-Shu point of the Large Intestine

V 26.loc: On the lower back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 5th lumbar vertebra (L5), 1.5 cun lateral to the midline.
V 26.act: Strengthens the lower back, regulates the lower abdomen (Lower Energizer) and urination, eliminates Dampness.
V 26.ind: low back pain; bloating; diarrhea; frequent urination; difficult urination; bedwetting; intense thirst with weight loss (wasting and thirsting disorder)
cats: Back-Shu point of the Gate of Origin

V 27.loc: On the sacrum, level with the 1st posterior sacral foramen, 1.5 cun lateral to the median sacral crest.
V 27.act: Separates the clear from the turbid, regulates the Small Intestine and Bladder, drains Damp-Heat.
V 27.ind: dark, scanty or painful urination; blood in the urine; bedwetting; diarrhea and dysentery; lower abdominal pain; vaginal discharge; seminal emissions; sacroiliac and low back pain
cats: Back-Shu point of the Small Intestine

V 28.loc: On the sacrum, 1.5 cun on each side of the midline, level with the 2nd sacral hole.
V 28.act: Back-Shu point of the Bladder: regulates urination.
V 28.fn: Regulates the Bladder and promotes urination, drains Damp-Heat from the lower abdomen, strengthens the lower back.
V 28.locp: On the sacrum, level with the 2nd posterior sacral foramen, 1.5 cun lateral to the median sacral crest.
V 28.ind: difficult urination; burning urination; urinary retention; frequent urination; bedwetting; diarrhea; constipation; pain and stiffness of the lower back and sacrum; genital pain; sciatica

V 29.loc: On the sacrum, level with the 3rd posterior sacral foramen, 1.5 cun lateral to the median sacral crest.
V 29.act: Strengthens the lower back, dispels Cold, stops diarrhea.
V 29.ind: lumbosacral pain and stiffness; dysentery; diarrhea; hernia; lower abdominal pain; intense thirst with weight loss (wasting and thirsting disorder)

V 30.loc: On the sacrum, level with the 4th posterior sacral foramen, 1.5 cun lateral to the median sacral crest.
V 30.act: Regulates menstruation and stops vaginal discharge, secures Essence (Jing), strengthens the lower back.
V 30.ind: vaginal discharge; irregular periods; seminal emissions; bedwetting; hernia; lumbosacral and tailbone pain; sciatica; difficult urination and defecation
V 30.ci: Moxibustion is forbidden in the classical lists of points not to be moxibusted.

V 31.loc: On the sacrum, in the 1st posterior sacral foramen, about midway between the posterior superior iliac spine and the midline.
V 31.act: Regulates the lower abdomen (Lower Energizer), regulates menstruation and stops vaginal discharge, promotes urination and defecation, strengthens the lower back and knees.
V 31.ind: irregular periods; vaginal discharge; uterine prolapse; infertility; impotence; difficult urination; constipation; lumbosacral pain; cold, painful knees
V 31.ci: Contraindicated in pregnancy (strongly stimulates the uterus).

V 32.loc: On the sacrum, in the 2nd posterior sacral foramen, slightly medial and inferior to the posterior superior iliac spine.
V 32.act: Regulates menstruation and the lower abdomen, moves Qi and Blood in the pelvis and relieves pain, promotes urination, strengthens the lower back and legs.
V 32.ind: painful periods; irregular periods; vaginal discharge; infertility; impotence and seminal emissions; difficult urination; lumbosacral pain; sciatica; numb legs; long or difficult labor
V 32.ci: Contraindicated in pregnancy, except to help labor progress at term.

V 33.loc: On the sacrum, in the 3rd posterior sacral foramen, between BL 32 and BL 34.
V 33.act: Regulates the lower abdomen (Lower Energizer), promotes urination and defecation, regulates menstruation, strengthens the lower back.
V 33.ind: irregular periods; vaginal discharge; infertility; difficult urination; constipation; diarrhea; lumbosacral pain
V 33.ci: Contraindicated in pregnancy (strongly stimulates the uterus).

V 34.loc: On the sacrum, in the 4th posterior sacral foramen, just lateral to the sacral hiatus.
V 34.act: Regulates the lower abdomen (Lower Energizer), promotes urination and defecation, strengthens the lower back.
V 34.ind: lower abdominal pain; difficult urination; constipation; blood in the stools; vaginal discharge; lumbosacral pain spreading to the genitals
V 34.ci: Contraindicated in pregnancy (strongly stimulates the uterus).

V 35.loc: At the bottom of the buttock, 0.5 cun to each side of the tip of the tailbone (coccyx).
V 35.act: Drains Damp-Heat from the lower body, treats hemorrhoids, regulates the lower abdomen (Lower Energizer).
V 35.ind: hemorrhoids; blood in the stools; diarrhea and dysentery; vaginal discharge; impotence; itching and dampness of the genitals; tailbone pain

V 36.loc: On the back of the thigh, at the midpoint of the gluteal fold.
V 36.act: Frees the channel and relieves pain, strengthens the lower back and legs, treats hemorrhoids.
V 36.ind: pain of the lower back, sacrum, buttock and thigh; sciatica; weakness or paralysis of the legs; hemorrhoids; constipation; difficult urination
V 36.ci: Moxibustion is forbidden in the classical lists of points not to be moxibusted.

V 37.loc: On the back of the thigh, 6 cun below the gluteal fold, between the biceps femoris and semitendinosus muscles, on the line from BL 36 to BL 40.
V 37.act: Frees the channel, relieves pain in the lower back and leg, strengthens the lower back.
V 37.ind: low back pain that prevents bending forward or backward; pain spreading down the back of the thigh; sciatica; pain and swelling of the thigh; weakness or paralysis of the legs; low back strain
V 37.ci: Moxibustion is forbidden in the classical lists of points not to be moxibusted.

V 38.loc: On the back of the knee, 1 cun above the popliteal crease, just medial to the biceps femoris tendon (1 cun above BL 39).
V 38.act: Relaxes the tendons and frees the channel, clears Heat and promotes urination.
V 38.ind: pain and tightness in the back of the knee; numbness of the buttock and thigh; calf cramps; constipation; urinary retention; burning urination

V 39.loc: On the popliteal crease, at its lateral end, at the medial border of the biceps femoris tendon.
V 39.act: Opens the water passages and promotes urination, regulates the Triple Energizer, relaxes the tendons of the knee and back.
V 39.ind: urinary retention; difficult urination; bedwetting; edema; distension of the lower abdomen; stiffness and pain of the lower back; cramps and pain of the knee and calf
cats: Lower He-Sea point of the Triple Energizer

V 40.loc: In the middle of the crease behind the knee.
V 40.act: Soothes the back and knees, cools the Blood.
V 40.fn: Benefits the lower back and knees, frees the channel, cools Blood and dispels Blood Stasis, clears Summer-Heat, promotes urination.
V 40.locp: At the midpoint of the popliteal crease (behind the knee), between the tendons of the biceps femoris and semitendinosus.
V 40.ind: acute or chronic low back pain; sciatica; knee pain and stiffness; hemiplegia; vomiting and diarrhea from heatstroke; acute abdominal pain; difficult urination, bedwetting; skin disorders from Blood Heat (eczema, boils, erysipelas); nosebleeds
V 40.ci: The popliteal artery and vein lie beneath the point: do not needle too deeply or manipulate roughly. Bleeding is done only on small visible superficial veins. Moxibustion is forbidden in the classical lists of points not to be moxibusted.
cats: Lower He-Sea point of the Bladder

V 41.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 2nd thoracic vertebra (T2), 3 cun lateral to the midline (at the medial border of the shoulder blade).
V 41.act: Expels Wind and Cold, relaxes the tendons and frees the channel in the neck, shoulders and back.
V 41.ind: stiff, painful neck; wry neck from Wind-Cold; tight shoulders and upper back; numbness of the arm and elbow; pain between the shoulder blades; colds with stiffness
V 41.ci: Risk of pneumothorax (the lung lies close to the surface on this line): needle obliquely, 0.3 to 0.5 cun, never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 42.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 3rd thoracic vertebra (T3), 3 cun lateral to the midline (level with BL 13).
V 42.act: Tonifies and nourishes the Lung, descends Lung Qi, calms cough and wheezing, settles the corporeal soul (Po).
V 42.ind: cough; asthma; shortness of breath; tuberculosis and chronic lung disease; afternoon fever; stiff neck; shoulder and back pain; prolonged sadness and grief
V 42.ci: Risk of pneumothorax (the lung lies close to the surface on this line): needle obliquely, 0.3 to 0.5 cun, never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 43.loc: On the back, 3 cun on each side of the spine, below the 4th thoracic vertebra, at the inner edge of the shoulder blade.
V 43.act: Tonifies Qi and Yin in long-standing weakness.
V 43.fn: Tonifies Qi, nourishes Yin and Essence (Jing), strengthens the Lung, Heart, Spleen and Kidney, calms the Shen (mind); a major point for chronic exhaustion, especially with moxibustion.
V 43.locp: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 4th thoracic vertebra (T4), 3 cun lateral to the midline, at the medial border of the shoulder blade (arms crossed in front to move the shoulder blade aside).
V 43.ind: chronic fatigue and exhaustion; chronic cough; asthma; tuberculosis; night sweats; coughing up blood; poor memory; palpitations; seminal emissions; weak digestion with weight loss; pain between the shoulder blades
V 43.ci: Risk of pneumothorax (the lung lies close to the surface on this line): needle obliquely, 0.3 to 0.5 cun, never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 44.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 5th thoracic vertebra (T5), 3 cun lateral to the midline (level with BL 15).
V 44.act: Calms the Shen (mind), opens the chest and descends rebellious Qi.
V 44.ind: anxiety; insomnia; palpitations; chest pain and tightness; cough; asthma; stiffness and pain of the back and shoulders
V 44.ci: Risk of pneumothorax (the lung lies close to the surface on this line): needle obliquely, 0.3 to 0.5 cun, never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 45.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 6th thoracic vertebra (T6), 3 cun lateral to the midline (level with BL 16).
V 45.act: Releases the exterior and expels Wind-Heat, descends Lung Qi, moves Qi and relieves pain.
V 45.ind: cough; asthma; fever without sweating; intermittent fevers; shoulder and back pain spreading to the ribs; rib pain; dizziness; nosebleeds
V 45.ci: Risk of pneumothorax (the lung lies close to the surface on this line): needle obliquely, 0.3 to 0.5 cun, never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 46.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 7th thoracic vertebra (T7), 3 cun lateral to the midline (roughly level with the lower tip of the shoulder blade).
V 46.act: Frees the diaphragm, harmonizes the Stomach and descends rebellious Qi.
V 46.ind: hiccups; belching; vomiting; difficulty swallowing; tightness in the chest; stiffness and pain of the back
V 46.ci: Risk of pneumothorax (the lung lies close to the surface on this line): needle obliquely, 0.3 to 0.5 cun, never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 47.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 9th thoracic vertebra (T9), 3 cun lateral to the midline (level with BL 18).
V 47.act: Spreads Liver Qi, relaxes the tendons, settles the ethereal soul (Hun).
V 47.ind: pain and distension under the ribs; chest and back pain; vomiting; diarrhea; borborygmi; low mood and lack of direction; fears and restless dreams; muscle tightness
V 47.ci: Risk of pneumothorax (the lung lies close to the surface on this line): needle obliquely, 0.3 to 0.5 cun, never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 48.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 10th thoracic vertebra (T10), 3 cun lateral to the midline (level with BL 19).
V 48.act: Drains Damp-Heat from the Liver and Gallbladder, harmonizes the Spleen and Stomach.
V 48.ind: jaundice; bitter taste; pain under the ribs; borborygmi; diarrhea; abdominal pain; dark or difficult urination
V 48.ci: Risk of pneumothorax (the lung lies close to the surface on this line): needle obliquely, 0.3 to 0.5 cun, never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 49.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 11th thoracic vertebra (T11), 3 cun lateral to the midline (level with BL 20).
V 49.act: Tonifies the Spleen, transforms Dampness, clears Heat; supports thinking and concentration (Yi).
V 49.ind: bloating; borborygmi; vomiting; diarrhea; jaundice; intense thirst (wasting and thirsting disorder); poor appetite; poor concentration and overthinking; back pain
V 49.ci: Risk of pneumothorax (the lung lies close to the surface on this line): needle obliquely, 0.3 to 0.5 cun, never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 50.loc: On the back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12), 3 cun lateral to the midline (level with BL 21).
V 50.act: Harmonizes the Stomach and Spleen, resolves food stagnation.
V 50.ind: epigastric distension and pain; poor appetite; difficult digestion; indigestion in children; vomiting; edema; constipation; back pain
V 50.ci: Risk of pneumothorax (the lung lies close to the surface on this line): needle obliquely, 0.3 to 0.5 cun, never deeply and perpendicularly.

V 51.loc: On the lower back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 1st lumbar vertebra (L1), 3 cun lateral to the midline (level with BL 22).
V 51.act: Regulates the Triple Energizer, disperses stagnation and masses, benefits the breasts.
V 51.ind: epigastric pain; abdominal masses; constipation; breast disorders (engorgement, mastitis); pain under the ribs; low back pain
V 51.ci: Do not needle deeply (the kidney is close): needle obliquely, 0.5 to 0.8 cun.

V 52.loc: On the lower back, 3 cun from the spine (four finger-widths), level with the 2nd lumbar vertebra, i.e. at the waist.
V 52.act: “Residence of the Will”: strengthens the Kidney, willpower and sexual health.
V 52.fn: Tonifies the Kidney and secures Essence (Jing), strengthens willpower (Zhi) and the lower back, promotes urination.
V 52.locp: On the lower back, level with the lower border of the spinous process of the 2nd lumbar vertebra (L2), 3 cun lateral to the midline (level with BL 23, roughly at the waist).
V 52.ind: low back pain and stiffness; impotence; seminal emissions; premature ejaculation; difficult urination; edema; pain and swelling of the genitals; lack of drive and discouragement
V 52.ci: Do not needle deeply (the kidney is close): needle obliquely, 0.5 to 0.8 cun.

V 53.loc: On the buttock, level with the 2nd posterior sacral foramen, 3 cun lateral to the median sacral crest (level with BL 28 and BL 32).
V 53.act: Promotes urination, regulates the lower abdomen (Lower Energizer), strengthens the lower back.
V 53.ind: urinary retention; difficult urination; distension and swelling of the lower abdomen; borborygmi; constipation; lumbosacral pain and stiffness

V 54.loc: On the buttock, level with the 4th posterior sacral foramen (level with the sacral hiatus), 3 cun lateral to the median sacral crest.
V 54.act: Strengthens the lower back and legs, frees the channel and relieves pain, promotes urination and treats hemorrhoids.
V 54.ind: lumbosacral pain; sciatica; buttock pain; weakness, wasting or paralysis of the legs; hemorrhoids; difficult urination; constipation; genital pain
V 54.ci: The sciatic nerve runs deep beneath the point: if an electric sensation shoots down the leg, withdraw the needle slightly and do not persist.

V 55.loc: On the back of the leg, 2 cun below the popliteal crease (below BL 40), between the medial and lateral heads of the gastrocnemius muscle.
V 55.act: Frees the channel and relieves pain, stops uterine bleeding, relieves genital pain.
V 55.ind: low back pain spreading down the leg; leg pain and weakness; paralysis of the legs; uterine bleeding; vaginal discharge; genital pain; hernia

V 56.loc: On the back of the leg, 5 cun below the popliteal crease, between the two bellies of the gastrocnemius muscle, midway between BL 55 and BL 57.
V 56.act: Relaxes the tendons, frees the channel, treats hemorrhoids.
V 56.ind: calf cramps and pain; low back pain; sciatica; heel pain; hemorrhoids; constipation; nosebleeds
V 56.ci: Listed among the points forbidden to needling in classical texts; it is needled normally today, but moxibustion and massage remain gentle options.

V 57.loc: On the back of the leg, in the middle of the calf, in the hollow that appears below the two bulges of the muscle when you stand on tiptoe.
V 57.act: Relieves hemorrhoids, cramps and calf pain.
V 57.fn: Relaxes the tendons and eases cramps, frees the channel and relieves pain, treats hemorrhoids and regulates the intestines.
V 57.locp: On the back of the leg, in the middle of the calf, in the V-shaped hollow that appears below the two bellies of the gastrocnemius, where they join the Achilles tendon, when standing on tiptoe (about 8 cun below BL 40).
V 57.ind: hemorrhoids; constipation; rectal prolapse; calf cramps; leg pain and heaviness; low back pain; sciatica; heel pain; swollen, weak feet

V 58.loc: On the back and outer side of the leg, 7 cun above BL 60, between the lower border of the lateral head of the gastrocnemius and the Achilles tendon (about 1 cun lateral and inferior to BL 57).
V 58.act: Harmonizes above and below: expels Wind from the head, strengthens the Kidney and relieves back and leg pain; treats hemorrhoids.
V 58.ind: headache and dizziness; blocked nose and nosebleeds; low back pain; sciatica; weak, heavy legs; hemorrhoids; mental restlessness

V 59.loc: On the back and outer side of the leg, 3 cun above BL 60, between the fibula and the Achilles tendon.
V 59.act: Strengthens the back and legs, expels Wind and Dampness, frees the channel and regulates the Yang Motility Vessel (Yang Qiao).
V 59.ind: low back pain that makes standing for long difficult; sciatica; headache and heavy head; ankle pain and swelling; pain along the outer side of the leg; weakness or paralysis of the legs
cats: Xi-Cleft point of the Yang Qiao Mai

V 60.loc: In the hollow between the outer ankle bone and the Achilles tendon.
V 60.act: Soothes the back, neck and head.
V 60.fn: Expels Wind and frees the channel along its whole course, relieves pain of the head, neck, back and heel, descends Yang, strengthens the back and promotes labor.
V 60.locp: On the outer side of the ankle, in the depression between the tip (most prominent point) of the lateral malleolus and the Achilles tendon.
V 60.ind: occipital headache; stiff neck; dizziness; eye pain; nosebleeds; back pain and low back pain; sciatica; ankle and heel pain and swelling; childhood epilepsy; difficult labor and retained placenta
V 60.ci: Contraindicated in pregnancy (promotes descent of the fetus), except to help labor at term.

V 61.loc: On the outer side of the foot, directly below BL 60, on the lateral side of the calcaneus, at the border between the pale skin of the sole and the darker skin of the top of the foot.
V 61.act: Strengthens the bones and tendons, frees the channel and relieves pain, calms the Shen (mind).
V 61.ind: heel pain; weakness and wasting of the legs; low back pain; cramps; swollen feet; epilepsy; fainting

V 62.loc: In the hollow just below the tip of the outer ankle bone.
V 62.act: Calms the mind, soothes the neck and back.
V 62.fn: Opens and regulates the Yang Motility Vessel (Yang Qiao), calms the Shen (mind), expels internal and external Wind, relaxes the tendons and relieves pain of the head, neck and back.
V 62.locp: On the outer side of the foot, directly below the tip of the lateral malleolus, in the depression between the lower border of the malleolus and the calcaneus.
V 62.ind: insomnia; epilepsy (especially daytime seizures); headache; dizziness; stiff neck; back and low back pain; red, painful eyes; facial paralysis; hemiplegia; ankle pain and swelling
V 62.ci: Moxibustion is forbidden in the classical lists of points not to be moxibusted.
cats: Opening (confluent) point of the Yang Qiao Mai, paired with SI 3
One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

V 63.loc: On the outer edge of the foot, anterior and inferior to the lateral malleolus, behind the tuberosity of the 5th metatarsal, in the depression below the cuboid bone.
V 63.act: Frees the channel and relieves acute pain, subdues Wind and convulsions, calms the Shen (mind).
V 63.ind: acute ankle and foot pain; sprained ankle; acute low back pain; headache; convulsions in children; epilepsy; calf cramps

V 64.loc: On the outer edge of the foot, just in front (toward the toes) of the tuberosity of the 5th metatarsal, at the border between the pale skin of the sole and the skin of the top of the foot.
V 64.act: Expels Wind, clears the head and eyes, calms the Shen (mind), strengthens the back and frees the channel.
V 64.ind: headache; stiff neck; dizziness; red eyes and clouded vision; nosebleeds; epilepsy; palpitations; low back pain; foot and leg pain

V 65.loc: On the outer edge of the foot, in the depression just behind the 5th metatarsophalangeal joint, at the border between the pale and darker skin.
V 65.act: Expels Wind, clears the head and eyes, clears Heat, frees the channel.
V 65.ind: headache; stiff neck; dizziness; red, painful eyes; deafness; epilepsy and mental agitation; fever and chills; low back pain; pain at the back of the leg; boils and abscesses

V 66.loc: On the outer edge of the foot, in the depression just in front of the 5th metatarsophalangeal joint, at the border between the pale and darker skin.
V 66.act: Clears the head, expels Wind and Heat, calms the Shen (mind).
V 66.ind: headache; heavy head; stiff neck; dizziness; blurred vision; nosebleeds; fear and restlessness; epilepsy; difficult digestion
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Bladder

V 67.loc: On the little toe, on its outer side, 0.1 cun proximal and lateral to the outer corner of the toenail.
V 67.act: Corrects malposition of the fetus and eases labor, expels Wind, clears the head and eyes, opens the nose.
V 67.ind: breech presentation (moxibustion); difficult labor; retained placenta; vertex and neck headache; eye pain; blocked nose and nosebleeds; fever without sweating; difficult urination
V 67.ci: Contraindicated in pregnancy, except to turn a breech baby (moxibustion, usually between weeks 32 and 35, with obstetric follow-up) or to ease labor at term.

Rn 1.loc: On the sole of the foot, in the hollow that forms when you curl your toes, at the front third of the sole.
Rn 1.act: Draws down what rises to the head, calms the mind, grounds you before sleep.
Rn 1.fn: Descends excess Yang and Heat from the head, calms the Shen, revives consciousness and rescues Yang; clears Heat and nourishes Kidney Yin.
Rn 1.locp: On the sole of the foot, in the deepest depression that appears when the toes are flexed, at the junction of the anterior third and posterior two thirds of the line from the base of the 2nd and 3rd toes to the heel.
Rn 1.ind: loss of consciousness, fainting; childhood convulsions, epilepsy; vertex headache; dizziness; insomnia, agitation; dry sore throat, loss of voice; burning soles; constipation; difficult urination
Rn 1.ci: Needling is very painful: reserve it for emergencies and Excess patterns; otherwise prefer acupressure or moxibustion.

Rn 2.loc: Inner edge of the foot, in the hollow below the bump of the navicular bone (in front of and below the ankle bone).
Rn 2.fn: Clears Deficiency-Heat, strengthens the Kidney and regulates the Lower Energizer; cools the throat and settles agitation.
Rn 2.locp: On the medial border of the foot, below the tuberosity of the navicular bone, at the border between the skin of the dorsum and that of the sole.
Rn 2.ind: night sweats; wasting-thirst (diabetes); sore throat; coughing blood; irregular menstruation; genital itching; uterine prolapse; nocturnal emissions, impotence; difficult urination; swollen, painful foot
Rn 2.ci: Classically, bleeding this point after needling is to be avoided.

Rn 3.loc: In the hollow between the inner ankle bone and the Achilles tendon, level with the tip of the ankle bone.
Rn 3.act: Yuan-Source point of the Kidney: tonifies Kidney Yin and Yang.
Rn 3.fn: Tonifies Kidney Yin, Yang and Essence (Jing), helps the Kidney grasp Qi, strengthens the lower back and knees; clears Deficiency-Heat and regulates the uterus.
Rn 3.locp: On the posteromedial side of the ankle, in the depression between the prominence of the medial malleolus and the Achilles tendon.
Rn 3.ind: tinnitus, deafness; dizziness; toothache, sore throat; cough, asthma; insomnia, poor memory; lower back pain; impotence, nocturnal emissions; frequent urination; irregular menstruation; wasting-thirst (diabetes); swollen, painful ankle
Rn 3.ci: The posterior tibial artery runs right beside the point: palpate it and avoid it.

Rn 4.loc: On the medial side of the foot, posteroinferior to the medial malleolus, above the calcaneus, in the depression anterior to the medial attachment of the Achilles tendon (about 0.5 cun below and slightly posterior to KI 3).
Rn 4.act: Strengthens the Kidney and helps it grasp Qi, lifts the spirit and dispels fear, regulates urination and bowel movements.
Rn 4.ind: asthma, shortness of breath; coughing blood; fearfulness, timidity; low spirits, desire to stay shut indoors; somnolence, mental dullness; urinary retention or difficult urination; constipation; lower back pain and stiffness; heel pain

Rn 5.loc: On the medial side of the foot, 1 cun directly below KI 3, in the depression anterior to the calcaneal tuberosity.
Rn 5.act: Regulates the Chong and Conception Vessels, activates Blood circulation, regulates menstruation and promotes urination; relieves acute pain.
Rn 5.ind: amenorrhea; irregular menstruation; painful menstruation; uterine prolapse; difficult urination; abdominal pain; blurred vision; heel pain

Rn 6.loc: In the hollow just below the tip of the inner ankle bone.
Rn 6.act: Nourishes Yin, moistens the throat and eyes, helps sleep.
Rn 6.fn: Nourishes Kidney Yin and clears Deficiency-Heat, moistens the throat, calms the Shen, regulates the Yin Motility Vessel (Yin Qiao) and the Lower Energizer, benefits the eyes.
Rn 6.locp: On the medial side of the ankle, 1 cun below the prominence of the medial malleolus, in the depression beneath it.
Rn 6.ind: dry, sore throat; sensation of a lump in the throat; insomnia; somnolence; epilepsy occurring at night; irregular menstruation, vaginal discharge; uterine prolapse; genital itching; frequent urination; constipation; dry, red eyes
cats: Opening (confluent) point of the Yin Qiao Mai, paired with LU 7

Rn 7.loc: 2 cun above KI 3, at the front edge of the Achilles tendon.
Rn 7.act: Tonifies the Kidney, regulates sweating and body fluids.
Rn 7.fn: Tonifies Kidney Yang and Yin, regulates the water passages and sweating, drains Dampness and Damp-Heat; strengthens the lower back.
Rn 7.locp: On the posteromedial side of the leg, 2 cun above the prominence of the medial malleolus, just anterior to the Achilles tendon.
Rn 7.ind: edema, swollen legs; night sweats; spontaneous sweating or absence of sweating; lower back pain; diarrhea, bloody stools; hemorrhoids; difficult or cloudy urination; cold, weak legs; dry mouth

Rn 8.loc: On the medial side of the leg, 2 cun above the prominence of the medial malleolus, in the depression posterior to the medial border of the tibia (0.5 cun anterior to KI 7).
Rn 8.act: Regulates the Chong and Conception Vessels, regulates menstruation and stops uterine bleeding; clears Damp-Heat from the Lower Energizer and regulates the intestines.
Rn 8.ind: irregular menstruation; uterine bleeding, heavy periods; amenorrhea; uterine prolapse; diarrhea, dysentery; constipation; painful, swollen testicles; hernia; pain on the inner side of the leg
cats: Xi-Cleft point of the Yin Qiao Mai

Rn 9.loc: On the posteromedial side of the leg, 5 cun above the prominence of the medial malleolus, between the soleus muscle and the Achilles tendon, on the line connecting KI 3 and KI 10.
Rn 9.act: Calms the Shen, transforms Phlegm and clears the Heart; regulates the Yin Linking Vessel (Yin Wei); relaxes the leg.
Rn 9.ind: mental agitation, manic behavior; epilepsy; vomiting of frothy fluid; palpitations, chest oppression; hernia, lower abdominal pain; calf cramps and pain; weak legs
cats: Xi-Cleft point of the Yin Wei Mai

Rn 10.loc: At the inner end of the crease behind the knee, between the two tendons you feel when you bend the knee slightly.
Rn 10.act: He-sea point of the Kidney: nourishes Kidney Yin, drains Damp-Heat from the lower body.
Rn 10.fn: Nourishes Kidney Yin, expels Damp-Heat from the Lower Energizer, benefits the knee.
Rn 10.locp: On the posteromedial side of the knee, on the popliteal crease, just lateral to the semitendinosus tendon (between the semitendinosus and semimembranosus tendons), with the knee slightly flexed.
Rn 10.ind: impotence; genital pain; itching of the scrotum; vaginal discharge; uterine bleeding; difficult or painful urination; lower abdominal pain radiating to the genitals; pain on the inner side of the knee
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Kidney

Rn 11.loc: On the lower abdomen, at the upper border of the pubic symphysis, 5 cun below the center of the umbilicus and 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior midline (beside CV 2).
Rn 11.act: Strengthens the Kidney, regulates the Lower Energizer and urination, benefits the genitals.
Rn 11.ind: urinary retention; incontinence, bedwetting; genital pain; impotence; nocturnal emissions; hernia; fullness and pain of the lower abdomen; vaginal discharge
Rn 11.ci: Have the patient empty the bladder before needling; needle cautiously (full bladder, thin patient); listed among the points forbidden to needling in classical texts; not advised during pregnancy.

Rn 12.loc: On the lower abdomen, 4 cun below the center of the umbilicus, 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior midline (beside CV 3).
Rn 12.act: Tonifies the Kidney, consolidates the Essence (Jing) and stops leakage; regulates the Lower Energizer.
Rn 12.ind: nocturnal emissions, premature ejaculation; impotence; penile pain; uterine prolapse; vaginal discharge; infertility; lower abdominal pain; red, painful eyes
Rn 12.ci: Have the patient empty the bladder before needling; not advised during pregnancy (lower abdomen).

Rn 13.loc: On the lower abdomen, 3 cun below the center of the umbilicus, 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior midline (beside CV 4).
Rn 13.act: Tonifies the Kidney, regulates the Chong and Conception Vessels, regulates menstruation and the water passages.
Rn 13.ind: irregular menstruation; painful menstruation; infertility; vaginal discharge; difficult urination; diarrhea; lower abdominal pain; sensation of Qi rushing up from the lower abdomen to the chest ("running piglet"); lower back pain
Rn 13.ci: Not advised during pregnancy (lower abdomen); needle cautiously in thin patients.

Rn 14.loc: On the lower abdomen, 2 cun below the center of the umbilicus, 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior midline (beside CV 5).
Rn 14.act: Regulates Qi and moves Blood, dissolves masses and Blood Stasis in the lower abdomen, regulates the water passages.
Rn 14.ind: abdominal masses; painful menstruation; irregular menstruation; uterine bleeding; infertility; postpartum abdominal pain; edema; diarrhea; nocturnal emissions
Rn 14.ci: Not advised during pregnancy (lower abdomen); needle cautiously in thin patients.

Rn 15.loc: On the lower abdomen, 1 cun below the center of the umbilicus, 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior midline (beside CV 7).
Rn 15.act: Regulates the Lower Energizer and the intestines, regulates menstruation.
Rn 15.ind: irregular menstruation; painful menstruation; lower abdominal pain; bloating; constipation; diarrhea; lower back pain; red, painful eyes
Rn 15.ci: Not advised during pregnancy (lower abdomen); needle cautiously in thin patients.

Rn 16.loc: On the abdomen, 0.5 cun lateral to the center of the umbilicus.
Rn 16.act: Tonifies the Kidney, regulates the intestines and moves Qi, relieves abdominal pain.
Rn 16.ind: abdominal pain, pain around the umbilicus; constipation; diarrhea, dysentery; bloating; vomiting; hernia; irregular menstruation; lower back pain
Rn 16.ci: Not advised during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy; needle cautiously in thin patients.

Rn 17.loc: On the upper abdomen, 2 cun above the center of the umbilicus, 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior midline (beside CV 10).
Rn 17.act: Regulates the intestines and Stomach, dispels accumulations and masses, relieves pain.
Rn 17.ind: abdominal pain; abdominal masses; bloating; constipation; diarrhea; poor appetite; red, painful eyes

Rn 18.loc: On the upper abdomen, 3 cun above the center of the umbilicus, 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior midline (beside CV 11).
Rn 18.act: Regulates the Stomach and descends rebellious Qi, regulates the Chong Vessel and dispels Blood Stasis.
Rn 18.ind: vomiting; hiccups; epigastric pain; constipation; infertility; postpartum abdominal pain; abdominal masses

Rn 19.loc: On the upper abdomen, 4 cun above the center of the umbilicus, 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior midline (beside CV 12).
Rn 19.act: Harmonizes the Stomach, descends rebellious Qi and regulates Qi in the abdomen.
Rn 19.ind: epigastric pain; bloating; nausea, vomiting; borborygmus; constipation; infertility; asthma, chest oppression

Rn 20.loc: On the upper abdomen, 5 cun above the center of the umbilicus, 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior midline (beside CV 13).
Rn 20.act: Harmonizes the Middle Energizer, unbinds the chest and transforms Phlegm, descends rebellious Qi.
Rn 20.ind: epigastric pain; vomiting; poor digestion; bloating; palpitations; chest pain; cough, asthma; sudden loss of voice

Rn 21.loc: On the upper abdomen, 6 cun above the center of the umbilicus, 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior midline (beside CV 14).
Rn 21.act: Harmonizes the Stomach and descends rebellious Qi, unbinds the chest, promotes lactation.
Rn 21.ind: nausea, vomiting; morning sickness; hiccups; epigastric pain; diarrhea; pain in the chest and below the ribs; insufficient lactation; breast abscess
Rn 21.ci: No deep needling: risk of injuring the liver (on the right), especially when it is enlarged.

Rn 22.loc: On the chest, in the 5th intercostal space, 2 cun lateral to the anterior midline.
Rn 22.act: Unbinds the chest, descends Lung and Stomach Qi, benefits the breasts.
Rn 22.ind: cough; asthma, shortness of breath; fullness of the chest and ribs; vomiting; poor appetite; breast abscess; nasal congestion
Rn 22.ci: Needle obliquely or transversely only: deep needling can cause a pneumothorax.

Rn 23.loc: On the chest, in the 4th intercostal space, 2 cun lateral to the anterior midline.
Rn 23.act: Unbinds the chest, descends Lung and Stomach Qi, benefits the breasts and settles the Shen.
Rn 23.ind: cough; asthma; fullness and pain of the chest and ribs; breast abscess; vomiting; poor appetite; palpitations, anxiety
Rn 23.ci: Needle obliquely or transversely only: deep needling can cause a pneumothorax.

Rn 24.loc: On the chest, in the 3rd intercostal space, 2 cun lateral to the anterior midline.
Rn 24.act: Unbinds the chest, descends rebellious Qi, benefits the breasts and calms the Shen.
Rn 24.ind: cough; asthma; fullness and pain of the chest and ribs; breast abscess; vomiting; anxiety, agitation; insomnia
Rn 24.ci: Needle obliquely or transversely only: deep needling can cause a pneumothorax.

Rn 25.loc: On the chest, in the 2nd intercostal space, 2 cun lateral to the anterior midline.
Rn 25.act: Unbinds the chest, descends Lung Qi, calms cough and settles the Shen.
Rn 25.ind: cough; asthma; chest oppression and pain; vomiting; poor appetite; agitation, anxiety; insomnia
Rn 25.ci: Needle obliquely or transversely only: deep needling can cause a pneumothorax.

Rn 26.loc: On the chest, in the 1st intercostal space, 2 cun lateral to the anterior midline.
Rn 26.act: Descends Lung Qi, transforms Phlegm, calms cough and asthma.
Rn 26.ind: cough; asthma; profuse sputum; fullness of the chest and ribs; poor appetite; vomiting
Rn 26.ci: Needle obliquely or transversely only: deep needling can cause a pneumothorax.

Rn 27.loc: Below the collarbone, 2 cun on each side of the midline.
Rn 27.act: Makes Lung Qi descend, calms coughing and breathlessness.
Rn 27.fn: Descends Lung Qi and rebellious Qi, calms cough and asthma, transforms Phlegm, harmonizes the Stomach.
Rn 27.locp: On the chest, at the lower border of the clavicle, 2 cun lateral to the anterior midline.
Rn 27.ind: cough; asthma, shortness of breath; chest pain; vomiting; poor appetite; hoarseness, sore throat; Qi rushing up into the chest
Rn 27.ci: Needle obliquely or transversely only: deep needling can cause a pneumothorax.

MC 1.loc: On the chest, in the fourth intercostal space, 5 cun lateral to the anterior midline (1 cun lateral to the nipple in men).
MC 1.act: Opens the chest, resolves Phlegm, subdues rebellious Qi, benefits the breasts and dissipates nodules.
MC 1.ind: chest oppression and pain; cough, shortness of breath; profuse Phlegm; rib pain; breast abscess, mastitis; insufficient lactation; swollen axillary lymph nodes; armpit pain
MC 1.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: needle obliquely or transversely along the intercostal space, never deeply.

MC 2.loc: On the anterior arm, 2 cun below the end of the anterior axillary fold, between the long and short heads of the biceps brachii.
MC 2.act: Opens the chest, moves Qi and Blood, stops pain.
MC 2.ind: heart pain; chest pain radiating to the back or arm; fullness of the ribs; cough; palpitations; pain of the inner arm

MC 3.loc: On the cubital crease, in the depression on the ulnar side of the biceps brachii tendon, with the elbow slightly flexed.
MC 3.act: Clears Heat from the Nutritive (Ying) and Blood levels, cools the Blood, harmonizes the Stomach and stops vomiting, calms the Shen.
MC 3.ind: high fever, heatstroke; agitation, thirst, dry mouth; palpitations, heart pain; vomiting, vomiting blood; acute diarrhea; eczema, rashes; pain of the elbow and arm; tremor of the hand and arm
MC 3.ci: The brachial artery runs right beside the point: palpate and avoid it. Bloodletting is done on the small visible veins.

MC 4.loc: On the anterior forearm, 5 cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease, between the tendons of palmaris longus and flexor carpi radialis (on the line from PC 3 to PC 7).
MC 4.act: Moves Blood and dispels Blood Stasis, stops acute heart pain, cools the Blood and stops bleeding, calms the Shen.
MC 4.ind: acute heart pain; chest pain; palpitations, fear; agitation, anxiety; fear of people; coughing blood; vomiting blood; nosebleed; boils
MC 4.ci: The median nerve lies beneath the point: if an electric sensation occurs, withdraw the needle slightly.

MC 5.loc: On the anterior forearm, 3 cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease, between the tendons of palmaris longus and flexor carpi radialis.
MC 5.act: Resolves Phlegm obstructing the Heart, calms the Shen, regulates Heart Qi, harmonizes the Stomach, treats malaria.
MC 5.ind: mental disorders, epilepsy; palpitations, heart pain; fear, anxiety; nausea, vomiting, stomach pain; malaria, intermittent fevers; loss of voice; irregular periods; pain of the arm and elbow
MC 5.ci: The median nerve lies beneath the point: if an electric sensation occurs, withdraw the needle slightly.

MC 6.loc: Inner side of the forearm, 2 cun above the wrist crease, between the two tendons.
MC 6.act: Opens the chest, makes Stomach Qi descend (nausea), calms the mind.
MC 6.fn: Opens the chest and regulates Heart Qi, harmonizes the Stomach and subdues its rebellious Qi, calms the Shen, regulates Liver Qi.
MC 6.locp: On the anterior forearm, 2 cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease, between the tendons of palmaris longus and flexor carpi radialis.
MC 6.ind: nausea, vomiting (including morning sickness and motion sickness); hiccups; epigastric pain; chest oppression and pain; palpitations, heart rhythm disorders; rib pain; insomnia, anxiety; sadness; dizziness; migraine; wrist pain, carpal tunnel syndrome
MC 6.ci: The median nerve lies beneath the point: if an electric sensation occurs, withdraw the needle slightly.
cats: Opening (confluent) point of the Yin Wei Mai, paired with SP 4

MC 7.loc: In the middle of the wrist crease, between the two tendons.
MC 7.act: Clears Heart Heat, calms the mind.
MC 7.fn: Clears Heart Heat, calms the Shen, harmonizes the Stomach and intestines, opens the chest.
MC 7.locp: At the middle of the palmar wrist crease, between the tendons of palmaris longus and flexor carpi radialis.
MC 7.ind: agitation, insomnia; anxiety, uncontrolled laughing or crying; palpitations, heart pain; chest oppression; epigastric pain, vomiting; bad breath, mouth ulcers; hot palms; eczema of the hands; wrist pain, carpal tunnel syndrome
MC 7.ci: The median nerve lies beneath the point: if an electric sensation occurs, withdraw the needle slightly.
cats: One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

MC 8.loc: In the center of the palm, between the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals, where the tip of your middle finger lands when you make a fist.
MC 8.fn: Clears Heart Fire and Stomach Heat, calms the Shen, restores consciousness.
MC 8.locp: On the palm, in the depression between the second and third metacarpal bones, proximal to the metacarpophalangeal joints, closer to the third, where the tip of the middle finger rests when making a fist (alternative: between the third and fourth metacarpals).
MC 8.ind: agitation, mental disorders; epilepsy; loss of consciousness; mouth and tongue ulcers; bad breath; heart pain; vomiting; hot, sweaty palms; fungal infection or eczema of the hands; nosebleed
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Pericardium
One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

MC 9.loc: At the centre of the tip of the middle finger (alternative: radial side of the middle finger, 0.1 cun proximal to the corner of the nail).
MC 9.act: Clears Heat, opens the orifices and restores consciousness, benefits the tongue.
MC 9.ind: loss of consciousness; stroke; heatstroke; high fever; heart pain; agitation; stiff, swollen tongue, difficulty speaking; childhood convulsions and night crying; hot palms

TR 1.loc: On the ulnar side of the ring finger, 0.1 cun proximal and medial to the ulnar corner of the nail.
TR 1.act: Clears Heat, benefits the tongue and throat, opens the orifices and restores consciousness.
TR 1.ind: sore throat; stiff tongue; febrile disease; headache; red eyes; tinnitus, deafness; dry mouth; agitation; loss of consciousness; elbow pain

TR 2.loc: On the dorsum of the hand, between the ring and little fingers, in the depression just proximal to the web margin, at the junction of the red and white skin (with a loose fist).
TR 2.act: Clears Heat, benefits the ears, calms the Shen.
TR 2.ind: tinnitus, deafness; headache; red, dry eyes; sore throat; pain of the teeth and gums; malaria; fear, palpitations; swelling and pain of the fingers and hand; arm pain

TR 3.loc: On the dorsum of the hand, between the fourth and fifth metacarpal bones, in the depression proximal to the fourth metacarpophalangeal joint (about 1 cun proximal to TE 2).
TR 3.act: Benefits the ears, clears Heat, regulates Shao Yang Qi, activates the channel and stops pain.
TR 3.ind: tinnitus, deafness; temporal headache; dizziness; red, painful eyes; sore throat; febrile disease; pain of the shoulder and back; pain of the elbow and arm; inability to flex or extend the fingers
cats: Tonification point of the Triple Energizer

TR 4.loc: On the dorsal wrist crease, in the depression on the ulnar side of the extensor digitorum tendon.
TR 4.act: Relaxes the tendons and benefits the wrist, clears Heat, generates fluids, harmonizes the Stomach.
TR 4.ind: pain and weakness of the wrist; pain of the shoulder and arm; intense thirst, dry mouth (diabetes); febrile disease; malaria; deafness; sore throat
cats: Yuan-Source point of the Triple Energizer

TR 5.loc: Back of the forearm, 2 cun above the wrist crease, between the two bones.
TR 5.act: Expels Wind-Heat, soothes the sides of the head and the ears.
TR 5.fn: Releases the exterior and expels Wind-Heat, clears Heat, benefits the head and ears, regulates Shao Yang Qi, activates the channel.
TR 5.locp: On the dorsal forearm, 2 cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease, at the midpoint of the interosseous space between the radius and ulna (opposite PC 6).
TR 5.ind: common cold with fever and chills; temporal headache, migraine; tinnitus, deafness; red, painful eyes; mumps; rib pain; neck stiffness; pain of the shoulder and arm; hand tremor; wrist pain
cats: Luo-Connecting point of the Triple Energizer
Opening (confluent) point of the Yang Wei Mai, paired with GB 41

TR 6.loc: Back of the forearm, 3 cun above the wrist crease, between the two bones.
TR 6.act: Moves Qi, helps the stools move down, soothes the ribs.
TR 6.fn: Regulates Qi and moves it through the three Energizers, opens the bowels, clears Heat, benefits the ribs.
TR 6.locp: On the dorsal forearm, 3 cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease, at the midpoint of the interosseous space between the radius and ulna.
TR 6.ind: constipation; pain of the ribs and flank; shingles over the ribs; sudden loss of voice; tinnitus, deafness; febrile disease without sweating; vomiting; pain of the shoulder and back; arm pain
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Triple Energizer

TR 7.loc: On the dorsal forearm, 3 cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease, just radial to the ulna (about one finger-width to the ulnar side of TE 6).
TR 7.act: Benefits the ears, activates the channel and stops pain.
TR 7.ind: deafness; tinnitus; epilepsy; pain of the skin and muscles; forearm pain; pain and weakness of the arm
cats: Xi-Cleft point of the Triple Energizer

TR 8.loc: On the dorsal forearm, 4 cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease, at the midpoint of the interosseous space between the radius and ulna.
TR 8.act: Activates the channel and stops pain, benefits the ears and voice.
TR 8.ind: sudden loss of voice; sudden deafness; toothache; pain of the forearm and arm; inability to move the arm; drowsiness, desire to lie down
TR 8.ci: Listed among the points forbidden to needling in the Zhen Jiu Da Cheng; in modern practice, moderate perpendicular needling or moxa.

TR 9.loc: On the dorsal forearm, 5 cun distal to the tip of the olecranon (7 cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease), at the midpoint of the interosseous space between the radius and ulna.
TR 9.act: Benefits the throat and voice, benefits the ears, activates the channel.
TR 9.ind: sudden loss of voice; sore throat; sudden deafness; toothache; shortness of breath; forearm pain

TR 10.loc: On the posterior arm, with the elbow flexed, in the depression 1 cun proximal to the tip of the olecranon (olecranon fossa).
TR 10.act: Resolves Phlegm and dissipates nodules, calms the Shen, regulates Qi, clears Heat, benefits the elbow.
TR 10.ind: swollen lymph nodes of the neck; goiter; epilepsy; sadness, depression; heart pain; cough; rib pain; migraine; deafness; elbow pain
cats: Sedation point of the Triple Energizer

TR 11.loc: On the posterior arm, 2 cun proximal to the tip of the olecranon (1 cun above TE 10), on the line joining the olecranon to the acromial angle.
TR 11.act: Expels Wind-Dampness, clears Damp-Heat, activates the channel.
TR 11.ind: pain of the shoulder and arm; inability to raise the arm; elbow pain; headache; eye pain; jaundice

TR 12.loc: On the posterior arm, 5 cun proximal to the tip of the olecranon, on the line joining the olecranon to the acromial angle.
TR 12.act: Activates the channel and stops pain, clears Heat.
TR 12.ind: headache; stiffness and pain of the neck; pain of the shoulder and arm; toothache; dizziness; epilepsy

TR 13.loc: On the posterior arm, below the posteroinferior border of the deltoid muscle, 3 cun below the acromial angle, on the line joining the acromion to the olecranon.
TR 13.act: Resolves Phlegm and dissipates nodules, activates the channel, benefits the shoulder.
TR 13.ind: goiter; swollen lymph nodes of the neck; pain of the shoulder and arm; weakness of the arm; inability to raise the arm; scapular pain

TR 14.loc: On the shoulder, in the depression between the acromial angle and the greater tubercle of the humerus; with the arm abducted, it is the posterior depression (the anterior one being LI 15).
TR 14.act: Expels Wind-Dampness, benefits the shoulder, activates the channel.
TR 14.ind: shoulder pain; frozen shoulder; inability to raise the arm; heaviness of the shoulder; paralysis of the upper limb; arm pain

TR 15.loc: In the scapular region, in the depression above the superior angle of the scapula (midway between GB 21 and SI 13).
TR 15.act: Expels Wind-Dampness, activates the channel, benefits the shoulder and neck, opens the chest.
TR 15.ind: pain of the shoulder and arm; stiffness and pain of the neck; pain in the supraclavicular fossa; fever without sweating; chest oppression; agitation
TR 15.ci: Risk of pneumothorax: do not needle deeply, especially forward.

TR 16.loc: On the lateral neck, level with the angle of the mandible, in the depression posterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
TR 16.act: Benefits the head and sense organs, descends Qi, reduces swelling.
TR 16.ind: sudden deafness; blurred vision; headache; dizziness; neck stiffness; facial swelling; goiter; swollen lymph nodes of the neck
TR 16.ci: Moxa classically forbidden. Shallow insertion only, avoiding the vessels of the neck.

TR 17.loc: Behind the earlobe, in the hollow between the jaw and the bone behind the ear.
TR 17.act: Soothes the ears and jaw, expels Wind.
TR 17.fn: Expels Wind, benefits the ears, clears Heat, unblocks the channel in the face and jaw.
TR 17.locp: Behind the earlobe, in the depression anterior to the tip of the mastoid process, between the mastoid and the ramus of the mandible.
TR 17.ind: tinnitus, deafness; ear pain and discharge; facial paralysis; pain and locking of the jaw; toothache; mumps; swollen cheeks; swollen lymph nodes of the neck; hiccups

TR 18.loc: Behind the ear, at the centre of the mastoid process, at the junction of the upper two thirds and lower third of the curved line following the helix from TE 20 to TE 17.
TR 18.act: Benefits the ears, calms fright and subdues Wind in children.
TR 18.ind: tinnitus, deafness; headache; childhood fright and convulsions; vomiting, diarrhea; blurred vision; pain behind the ear
TR 18.ci: Shallow transverse insertion or light bloodletting. Moxa classically forbidden.

TR 19.loc: Behind the ear, at the junction of the upper third and lower two thirds of the curved line following the helix from TE 20 to TE 17.
TR 19.act: Benefits the ears, calms fright and subdues Wind.
TR 19.ind: tinnitus, deafness; ear pain and discharge; headache; childhood fright and convulsions; vomiting; pain behind the ear
TR 19.ci: Listed among the points forbidden to needling in the Zhen Jiu Da Cheng: use only shallow transverse insertion.

TR 20.loc: On the head, just above the apex of the ear, at the hairline, when the auricle is folded forward.
TR 20.act: Benefits the ears, clears Heat and reduces swelling, benefits the eyes and teeth.
TR 20.ind: mumps; redness and swelling of the auricle; tinnitus; corneal opacity; red, painful eyes; toothache, swollen gums; neck stiffness; headache
TR 20.ci: Listed among the points forbidden to needling in the Zhen Jiu Da Cheng: use only shallow transverse insertion.

TR 21.loc: In front of the ear, in the depression between the supratragic notch and the condylar process of the mandible, which appears when the mouth is open (just above SI 19).
TR 21.act: Benefits the ears, clears Heat, benefits the teeth and jaw.
TR 21.ind: tinnitus, deafness; ear discharge, otitis; itching of the ear; toothache of the upper jaw; pain and locking of the jaw; stiffness of the lips
TR 21.ci: Needle with the mouth open. Moxa classically forbidden.

TR 22.loc: On the side of the head, behind the temporal hairline, in front of the root of the auricle, just posterior to the superficial temporal artery.
TR 22.act: Expels Wind, benefits the ears and nose, reduces swelling and stops pain.
TR 22.ind: headache, heaviness of the head; tinnitus; facial paralysis; clenched jaw; swelling and discharge of the nose; swelling of the face and neck
TR 22.ci: Avoid the superficial temporal artery (shallow oblique insertion). Moxa not advised (face, artery).

TR 23.loc: On the face, in the depression at the lateral end of the eyebrow.
TR 23.act: Expels Wind, brightens the eyes, stops pain.
TR 23.ind: one-sided headache, migraine; red, painful eyes; blurred vision; twitching of the eyelids; facial paralysis; dizziness; epilepsy; toothache
TR 23.ci: Moxa forbidden (close to the eye). Shallow transverse insertion.

VB 1.loc: On the face, in the depression 0.5 cun lateral to the outer canthus, at the lateral border of the orbit.
VB 1.act: Expels Wind-Heat, clears Fire, benefits the eyes and relieves pain.
VB 1.ind: red, swollen, painful eyes; tearing; photophobia; itchy eyes; blurred vision, cataract; temporal headache; facial paralysis
VB 1.ci: Moxibustion not advised (close to the eye); needle transversely backward, without entering the orbit.

VB 2.loc: In front of the ear, in the depression between the intertragic notch and the condylar process of the mandible, which deepens when the mouth is open (below SI 19).
VB 2.act: Opens the ears, expels exterior Wind, moves Qi in the channel and benefits the jaw.
VB 2.ind: deafness; tinnitus; ear discharge or earache; pain of the jaw joint; dislocation of the jaw; toothache; facial paralysis
VB 2.ci: Needle with the mouth open; the superficial temporal artery runs just in front.

VB 3.loc: In front of the ear, in the depression above the midpoint of the zygomatic arch, directly above ST 7.
VB 3.act: Expels Wind, opens the ears, benefits the teeth and jaw.
VB 3.ind: deafness; tinnitus; upper toothache; facial paralysis; lockjaw; migraine; dizziness
VB 3.ci: No deep needling (forbidden by classical texts); avoid the superficial temporal artery.

VB 4.loc: In the temporal hair, at the junction of the upper quarter and lower three quarters of the curved line connecting ST 8 and GB 7.
VB 4.act: Expels Wind-Heat, benefits the head and ears, relieves convulsions.
VB 4.ind: migraine; dizziness; tinnitus; pain at the outer corner of the eye; toothache; convulsions, epilepsy; neck pain

VB 5.loc: In the temporal hair, at the midpoint of the curved line connecting ST 8 and GB 7.
VB 5.act: Expels Wind, clears Heat, benefits the head and reduces facial swelling.
VB 5.ind: migraine; facial swelling; pain at the outer corner of the eye; toothache; nasal discharge; fever without sweating

VB 6.loc: In the temporal hair, at the junction of the upper three quarters and lower quarter of the curved line connecting ST 8 and GB 7.
VB 6.act: Expels Wind, clears Heat and benefits the head.
VB 6.ind: migraine; pain at the outer corner of the eye; tinnitus; toothache; sneezing; fever without sweating; facial swelling

VB 7.loc: On the temple, at the intersection of the vertical line along the posterior border of the sideburn hairline and the horizontal line through the apex of the ear.
VB 7.act: Expels Wind, benefits the head, jaw and mouth.
VB 7.ind: temporal headache; swollen cheek; lockjaw; sudden loss of voice; toothache; neck stiffness

VB 8.loc: Directly above the apex of the ear, 1.5 cun above the temporal hairline.
VB 8.act: Expels Wind, benefits the head, harmonizes the diaphragm and Stomach, stops vomiting.
VB 8.ind: migraine; dizziness; nausea and vomiting; ill effects of drunkenness; childhood convulsions; tinnitus; eye pain

VB 9.loc: Above the posterior border of the ear root, 2 cun above the hairline (about 0.5 cun posterior to GB 8).
VB 9.act: Clears Gallbladder Heat, expels Wind, calms the Shen and relieves convulsions.
VB 9.ind: headache; epilepsy; fright, palpitations; swollen, painful gums; goiter; tinnitus, deafness

VB 10.loc: Posterosuperior to the mastoid process, at the junction of the upper and middle thirds of the curved line from GB 9 to GB 12 that follows the contour of the ear.
VB 10.act: Expels Wind, benefits the head and ears, transforms Phlegm.
VB 10.ind: headache; tinnitus, deafness; toothache; goiter; swollen neck lymph nodes; cough; inability to raise the arm; weak legs

VB 11.loc: Posterosuperior to the mastoid process, at the junction of the middle and lower thirds of the curved line from GB 9 to GB 12.
VB 11.act: Expels Wind, opens the sense orifices (ears, eyes), benefits the head and neck.
VB 11.ind: headache; earache; tinnitus, deafness; neck pain and stiffness; bitter taste in the mouth; eye pain; dizziness

VB 12.loc: Behind the ear, in the depression posteroinferior to the mastoid process.
VB 12.act: Expels Wind, benefits the head and neck, calms the Shen.
VB 12.ind: headache; insomnia; neck pain and stiffness; swollen cheek; toothache; facial paralysis; pain behind the ear; epilepsy

VB 13.loc: On the head, 0.5 cun above the anterior hairline, 3 cun lateral to the midline (two thirds of the way from GV 24 to ST 8).
VB 13.act: Calms the Shen, gathers Essence (Jing) to the head, expels Wind and relieves epilepsy.
VB 13.ind: epilepsy; anxiety, excessive worry; agitation, mental disorders; headache; dizziness; childhood convulsions; hemiplegia; neck stiffness

VB 14.loc: On the forehead, 1 cun above the eyebrow, directly above the center of the pupil (eyes looking straight ahead).
VB 14.act: Expels Wind, benefits the eyes and relieves frontal pain.
VB 14.ind: frontal headache; eye pain; blurred vision; tearing in the wind; drooping eyelid; twitching eyelids; facial paralysis

VB 15.loc: On the head, 0.5 cun within the anterior hairline, directly above the center of the pupil (midway between GV 24 and ST 8).
VB 15.act: Benefits the eyes, expels Wind, benefits the head and nose, calms the Shen.
VB 15.ind: headache; dizziness; eye pain, tearing; blurred vision; nasal congestion; epilepsy; fever
VB 15.ci: Moxibustion classically forbidden on this point.

VB 16.loc: On the head, 1.5 cun within the anterior hairline, directly above the center of the pupil.
VB 16.act: Benefits the eyes, expels Wind and benefits the head.
VB 16.ind: headache; dizziness; red, painful eyes; blurred vision; facial swelling; nasal congestion; childhood convulsions

VB 17.loc: On the head, 2.5 cun within the anterior hairline, directly above the center of the pupil.
VB 17.act: Expels Wind, benefits the head and eases nausea.
VB 17.ind: headache; dizziness; toothache; nausea, vomiting; neck stiffness; stiff lips

VB 18.loc: On the head, 4 cun within the anterior hairline, directly above the center of the pupil.
VB 18.act: Expels Wind, benefits the head and opens the nose.
VB 18.ind: headache; dizziness; nasal congestion; nosebleed; rhinitis; eye pain; fever with chills
VB 18.ci: Listed among the points forbidden to needling in classical texts: today only subcutaneous needling is used.

VB 19.loc: On the back of the head, level with the upper border of the external occipital protuberance, directly above GB 20.
VB 19.act: Expels Wind, benefits the head and neck, calms the Shen.
VB 19.ind: occipital headache; neck stiffness; dizziness; epilepsy, fright; tinnitus; nasal congestion, nosebleed; eye pain

VB 20.loc: Below the back of the skull, in the hollow between the two large neck muscles.
VB 20.act: “Wind Pool”: expels Wind, eases headaches, dizziness and a stiff neck.
VB 20.fn: Expels exterior Wind and extinguishes interior Wind, subdues Liver Yang, clears the head, benefits the eyes and opens the ears and nose.
VB 20.locp: Below the occipital bone, in the depression between the upper attachments of the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles, level with GV 16.
VB 20.ind: headache, migraine; dizziness; neck stiffness; common cold, fever and chills; red eyes, blurred vision; tinnitus; nasal congestion; hypertension; insomnia; hemiplegia
VB 20.ci: Direct the needle toward the tip of the nose, at moderate depth (0.8 to 1.2 cun): deep needling upward and medially may reach the medulla oblongata and the vertebral artery.
cats: Meeting point with the Yang Wei Mai

VB 21.loc: On top of the shoulder, halfway between the base of the neck and the tip of the shoulder.
VB 21.act: Relaxes the shoulders and neck, makes Qi descend.
VB 21.fn: Moves Qi and Blood in the channel, descends rebellious Qi, transforms Phlegm, benefits the breasts and facilitates labor.
VB 21.locp: On top of the shoulder, at the midpoint of the line connecting the spinous process of C7 and the lateral end of the acromion, at the highest point of the trapezius.
VB 21.ind: neck and shoulder pain and stiffness; inability to raise the arm; breast abscess; insufficient lactation; difficult labor, retained placenta; swollen neck lymph nodes; cough, asthma; hypertension
VB 21.ci: Forbidden during pregnancy; no deep or perpendicular needling: the apex of the lung lies just beneath (pneumothorax); risk of fainting with overly strong stimulation.

VB 22.loc: On the lateral chest, in the 4th intercostal space, on the midaxillary line.
VB 22.act: Unbinds the chest and ribs, moves Qi in the channel, benefits the armpit and arm.
VB 22.ind: chest fullness; rib pain; swollen armpit, axillary lymph nodes; inability to raise the arm; cough; chills and fever
VB 22.ci: Moxibustion classically forbidden; needle only obliquely or transversely (risk of pneumothorax).

VB 23.loc: On the lateral chest, in the 4th intercostal space, 1 cun anterior to the midaxillary line (1 cun anterior to GB 22).
VB 23.act: Unbinds the chest, descends Lung and Stomach Qi, benefits the ribs.
VB 23.ind: chest fullness; asthma, shortness of breath; rib pain; vomiting; acid regurgitation; frequent sighing; insomnia
VB 23.ci: Needle obliquely or transversely only: deep needling can cause a pneumothorax.

VB 24.loc: On the chest, in the 7th intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the anterior midline (usually directly below the nipple in men).
VB 24.act: Benefits the Gallbladder and drains Damp-Heat, moves Liver Qi, harmonizes the Middle Energizer and descends rebellious Qi.
VB 24.ind: pain below the ribs; jaundice; bitter taste in the mouth; nausea, vomiting; acid regurgitation; hiccups; frequent sighing; sadness, low mood
VB 24.ci: Needle only obliquely or transversely: risk of pneumothorax and, on the right, of injury to the liver.

VB 25.loc: On the lateral abdomen, below the free end of the 12th rib.
VB 25.act: Strengthens the Kidney and lower back, regulates the water passages and promotes urination, regulates the intestines.
VB 25.ind: lower back pain; pain of the ribs and flanks; difficult urination; edema; bloating; borborygmus; diarrhea; vomiting
VB 25.ci: No deep needling: the kidney lies beneath.

VB 26.loc: On the lateral abdomen, below the free end of the 11th rib, level with the umbilicus (directly below LR 13).
VB 26.act: Regulates the Girdle Vessel (Dai Mai), drains Damp-Heat, regulates menstruation and stops vaginal discharge.
VB 26.ind: white or yellow vaginal discharge; irregular menstruation; amenorrhea; lower abdominal pain; hernia; uterine prolapse; pain of the lower back and flanks

VB 27.loc: On the lower abdomen, 3 cun below the umbilicus, just medial to the anterior superior iliac spine.
VB 27.act: Regulates the Girdle Vessel and the Lower Energizer, transforms Dampness, relieves pain.
VB 27.ind: vaginal discharge; uterine prolapse; hernia; lower abdominal pain; lower back and hip pain; constipation; tenesmus

VB 28.loc: On the lower abdomen, 0.5 cun medioinferior to the anterior superior iliac spine (medioinferior to GB 27).
VB 28.act: Regulates the Girdle Vessel and the Lower Energizer, transforms Dampness and holds up the lower abdominal organs.
VB 28.ind: vaginal discharge; uterine prolapse; hernia; lower abdominal pain; hip and lower back pain; edema; vomiting, poor appetite

VB 29.loc: On the hip, at the midpoint of the line connecting the anterior superior iliac spine and the prominence of the greater trochanter.
VB 29.act: Expels Wind-Dampness, moves Qi and Blood in the channel, benefits the hip and leg.
VB 29.ind: hip pain and stiffness; lower back pain radiating to the leg; sciatica; paralysis or weakness of the leg; numbness of the thigh; hernia

VB 30.loc: On the buttock, at the junction of the lateral third and medial two thirds of the line connecting the prominence of the greater trochanter and the sacral hiatus (patient lying on the side with the hip flexed).
VB 30.act: Moves Qi and Blood in the channel, expels Wind-Dampness, benefits the hip, lower back and leg.
VB 30.ind: hip pain; sciatica; lower back pain radiating down the leg; paralysis, atrophy or numbness of the leg; hemiplegia; knee pain; hives
VB 30.ci: Deep needling (2 to 3 cun) near the sciatic nerve: stop manipulating if an electric sensation shoots down the leg.

VB 31.loc: On the lateral thigh, in the depression posterior to the iliotibial band, where the tip of the middle finger rests when standing with the arms hanging alongside the thigh (about 9 cun above the popliteal crease in the WHO standard; 7 cun in older manuals).
VB 31.act: Expels Wind, relieves itching, relaxes the sinews and moves Qi in the leg.
VB 31.ind: itching all over the body, hives; pain on the outer side of the thigh; numbness of the leg; weakness or paralysis of the leg; hemiplegia; sciatica; knee pain

VB 32.loc: On the lateral thigh, posterior to the iliotibial band, 7 cun above the popliteal crease in the WHO 2008 standard, i.e. 2 cun below GB 31 (5 cun in older manuals).
VB 32.act: Expels Wind, Cold and Dampness, moves Qi and Blood in the channel, relaxes the sinews.
VB 32.ind: pain and numbness on the outer side of the thigh; weakness or paralysis of the leg; hemiplegia; sciatica; cramps; knee pain

VB 33.loc: On the lateral side of the knee, in the depression between the biceps femoris tendon and the iliotibial band, posterosuperior to the lateral epicondyle of the femur (about 3 cun above GB 34).
VB 33.act: Relaxes the sinews, expels Wind-Dampness and benefits the knee.
VB 33.ind: swollen, painful knee; stiffness and contracture of the tendons behind the knee; difficulty bending the knee; numbness of the leg; calf cramps; weak legs
VB 33.ci: Moxibustion classically forbidden on this point.

VB 34.loc: Outer side of the leg, in the hollow in front of and below the head of the fibula.
VB 34.act: Meeting point of the tendons: relaxes the tendons, frees the Liver and Gallbladder.
VB 34.fn: Spreads Liver Qi and benefits the Gallbladder, drains Damp-Heat, relaxes the sinews and benefits the joints, harmonizes the Shaoyang.
VB 34.locp: On the lateral side of the leg, in the depression anterior and inferior to the head of the fibula.
VB 34.ind: pain below the ribs; bitter taste; nausea, vomiting; jaundice; knee pain and stiffness; cramps, contractures; hemiplegia; numbness of the leg; shoulder stiffness; constipation
cats: Lower He-Sea point of the Gallbladder

VB 35.loc: On the lateral side of the leg, 7 cun above the prominence of the lateral malleolus, at the posterior border of the fibula.
VB 35.act: Moves Qi in the channel, relieves acute pain, calms the Shen; regulates the Yang Linking Vessel (Yang Wei).
VB 35.ind: pain on the outer side of the leg; knee pain; sciatica; weakness or paralysis of the leg; fullness of the chest and ribs; swollen throat; fright, mental agitation
cats: Xi-Cleft point of the Yang Wei Mai

VB 36.loc: On the lateral side of the leg, 7 cun above the prominence of the lateral malleolus, at the anterior border of the fibula (level with GB 35).
VB 36.act: Moves Qi in the channel, relieves acute pain, clears Heat and calms the Shen.
VB 36.ind: neck pain; chest and rib pain; pain on the outer side of the leg; weak legs; epilepsy; dog bites (classical indication)

VB 37.loc: On the lateral side of the leg, 5 cun above the prominence of the lateral malleolus, at the anterior border of the fibula.
VB 37.act: Benefits the eyes, moves Liver Qi, expels Wind-Dampness and benefits the leg.
VB 37.ind: eye pain; blurred vision; night blindness; itchy eyes; swollen, painful breasts; pain on the outer side of the leg; atrophy or weakness of the leg

VB 38.loc: On the lateral side of the leg, 4 cun above the prominence of the lateral malleolus, at the anterior border of the fibula.
VB 38.act: Clears Gallbladder Heat, moves Qi in the channel, benefits the sinews and bones.
VB 38.ind: migraine; pain at the outer corner of the eye; bitter taste; armpit pain; swollen neck lymph nodes; chest and rib pain; pain on the outer side of the leg; hemiplegia; wandering joint pain

VB 39.loc: 3 cun above the tip of the outer ankle bone, at the front edge of the fibula.
VB 39.act: Meeting point of marrow: nourishes the marrow and bones.
VB 39.fn: Nourishes the Marrow and bones, expels Wind-Dampness, clears Gallbladder Fire and moves Qi in the channel.
VB 39.locp: On the lateral side of the leg, 3 cun above the prominence of the lateral malleolus, at the anterior border of the fibula.
VB 39.ind: hemiplegia; neck stiffness; pain on the outer side of the leg; weak legs; fullness of the chest and ribs; sore throat; nosebleed; dizziness, tinnitus

VB 40.loc: In the hollow in front of and below the outer ankle bone.
VB 40.act: Frees the Liver and Gallbladder, soothes the ankle and the ribs.
VB 40.fn: Spreads Liver Qi, clears Damp-Heat from the Gallbladder, moves Qi in the channel and benefits the joints.
VB 40.locp: Anteroinferior to the lateral malleolus, in the depression lateral to the extensor digitorum longus tendon.
VB 40.ind: swollen, painful ankle, sprain; chest and rib pain; frequent sighing; neck pain; blurred vision, cataract; sciatica; hernia; intermittent fevers

VB 41.loc: Top of the foot, in the hollow in front of where the 4th and 5th metatarsals meet.
VB 41.act: Moves Liver Qi, soothes the temples and tender breasts.
VB 41.fn: Spreads Liver Qi, drains Damp-Heat, benefits the breasts and eyes, regulates the Girdle Vessel (Dai Mai).
VB 41.locp: On the dorsum of the foot, distal to the junction of the bases of the 4th and 5th metatarsals, in the depression lateral to the extensor tendon of the 5th toe.
VB 41.ind: migraine; pain at the outer corner of the eye; dizziness; pain below the ribs; tender, painful breasts, breast abscess; irregular menstruation; swollen neck lymph nodes; swollen, painful foot; intermittent fevers
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Gallbladder
Opening (confluent) point of the Dai Mai, paired with TE 5

VB 42.loc: On the dorsum of the foot, between the 4th and 5th metatarsals, in the depression just proximal to the 4th metatarsophalangeal joint, medial to the extensor tendon of the 5th toe.
VB 42.act: Spreads Liver and Gallbladder Qi, clears Heat, benefits the breasts, eyes and ears.
VB 42.ind: swollen breasts, breast abscess; rib pain; red, painful eyes; tinnitus; swollen armpit; red, swollen top of the foot
VB 42.ci: Moxibustion classically forbidden on this point.

VB 43.loc: Top of the foot, between the 4th and 5th toes, at the edge of the web.
VB 43.act: Subdues Liver Yang, soothes the temples and ears.
VB 43.fn: Clears Gallbladder Heat and Fire, subdues Liver Yang, benefits the head, eyes and ears, drains Damp-Heat.
VB 43.locp: On the dorsum of the foot, between the 4th and 5th toes, just proximal to the web margin, at the border between the skin of the dorsum and that of the sole.
VB 43.ind: headache, migraine; dizziness; tinnitus, deafness; pain at the outer corner of the eye; pain below the ribs; breast abscess; febrile diseases without sweating; swollen, painful top of the foot

VB 44.loc: At the outer corner of the 4th toenail, 0.1 cun from the corner of the nail.
VB 44.act: Well point of the Gallbladder: calms an agitated mind, nightmares and headaches.
VB 44.fn: Clears Heat and Wind from the Gallbladder, clears the head and the sense orifices, calms the Shen.
VB 44.locp: On the 4th toe, lateral side (toward the 5th toe), 0.1 cun from the corner of the toenail.
VB 44.ind: migraine; red, painful eyes; deafness, tinnitus; sore throat; nightmares, insomnia; agitation; rib pain; fever without sweating; cough

F 1.loc: On the big toe, outer side (toward the 2nd toe), 2 mm from the corner of the nail.
F 1.act: Warms and frees the Liver meridian, eases pain in the lower belly and genitals.
F 1.fn: Regulates Liver Qi, frees the channel in the lower abdomen and genitals, stops uterine bleeding, revives consciousness and calms the Shen.
F 1.locp: On the big toe, lateral side (toward the 2nd toe), 0.1 cun from the corner of the toenail.
F 1.ind: hernia, lower abdominal pain; swollen, painful testicles; uterine bleeding; uterine prolapse; bedwetting, urinary retention; loss of consciousness; epilepsy; somnolence
cats: Element point (horary point) of the Liver

F 2.loc: Top of the foot, between the big toe and the 2nd toe, at the edge of the web.
F 2.fn: Clears Liver Fire, subdues Liver Yang and extinguishes Wind, spreads Liver Qi, cools the Blood and stops bleeding.
F 2.locp: On the dorsum of the foot, between the big toe and the 2nd toe, just proximal to the web margin, at the border between the skin of the dorsum and that of the sole.
F 2.ind: headache, dizziness; red, painful eyes; irritability, anger; insomnia; pain below the ribs; heavy periods; burning urination; nosebleed; epilepsy, convulsions; swollen, painful top of the foot

F 3.loc: Top of the foot, in the hollow between the 1st and 2nd metatarsals, in front of where their bases meet.
F 3.act: Yuan-Source point of the Liver: frees Liver Qi, settles the Yang, calms the mind.
