F 3.fn: Subdues Liver Yang and extinguishes Wind, spreads Liver Qi, nourishes Liver Blood and Yin, clears the head and eyes, regulates menstruation and calms the Shen.
F 3.locp: On the dorsum of the foot, between the 1st and 2nd metatarsals, in the depression distal to the junction of their bases, over the pulse of the dorsalis pedis artery.
F 3.ind: headache, dizziness; hypertension; red, painful eyes; irritability, depressed mood; insomnia; pain below the ribs; irregular or painful menstruation; childhood convulsions; hernia; weakness or atrophy of the legs
F 3.ci: Locate the dorsalis pedis artery and avoid it when needling.

F 4.loc: On the anteromedial side of the ankle, in the depression medial to the tibialis anterior tendon, anterior to the medial malleolus (between SP 5 and ST 41).
F 4.act: Spreads Liver Qi, clears Liver Damp-Heat, regulates the Lower Energizer and benefits the ankle.
F 4.ind: hernia; genital pain; nocturnal emissions; difficult urination, urinary retention; jaundice; lower abdominal pain; lower back pain; swollen, painful ankle; cold feet

F 5.loc: 5 cun above the tip of the inner ankle bone, on the inner face of the shinbone.
F 5.act: Eliminates Damp-Heat from the genital area.
F 5.fn: Spreads Liver Qi, drains Damp-Heat from the genitals, regulates menstruation and relieves the sensation of a lump in the throat.
F 5.locp: On the anteromedial side of the leg, at the center of the medial surface of the tibia, 5 cun above the prominence of the medial malleolus.
F 5.ind: genital itching; vaginal discharge; irregular menstruation; swollen, painful testicles; hernia; difficult urination; persistent erection; sensation of a lump in the throat; painful, weak leg

F 6.loc: On the anteromedial side of the leg, at the center of the medial surface of the tibia, 7 cun above the prominence of the medial malleolus.
F 6.act: Spreads Liver Qi, regulates the Blood and stops bleeding, relieves acute pain.
F 6.ind: pain below the ribs; abdominal pain; hernia; uterine bleeding; prolonged lochia after childbirth; diarrhea; leg pain and weakness

F 7.loc: On the medial side of the leg, below the medial condyle of the tibia, 1 cun posterior to SP 9.
F 7.act: Expels Wind-Dampness, relaxes the sinews and benefits the knee.
F 7.ind: swollen, painful knee; difficulty bending or straightening the knee; kneecap pain; painful obstruction (Bi) of the leg; weak legs; sore throat

F 8.loc: Knee bent, at the inner end of the knee crease, in the hollow in front of the tendons.
F 8.act: Nourishes Liver Blood, soothes the knee.
F 8.fn: Nourishes Liver Blood and Yin, drains Damp-Heat from the Lower Energizer, benefits the genitals and the knee.
F 8.locp: With the knee flexed, at the medial end of the popliteal crease, in the depression anterior (medial) to the tendons of the semitendinosus and semimembranosus.
F 8.ind: uterine prolapse; genital itching and pain; vaginal discharge; nocturnal emissions, impotence; difficult urination; abdominal masses; amenorrhea, infertility; pain on the inner side of the knee

F 9.loc: On the medial thigh, between the gracilis and sartorius muscles, 4 cun above the base of the patella.
F 9.act: Regulates menstruation and the Lower Energizer, regulates urination.
F 9.ind: irregular menstruation; lower abdominal pain; bedwetting; difficult urination; lumbosacral pain radiating to the lower abdomen; pain on the inner side of the thigh

F 10.loc: On the medial thigh, 3 cun below ST 30, over the femoral artery.
F 10.act: Drains Damp-Heat, regulates the Lower Energizer and urination.
F 10.ind: lower abdominal distension; urinary retention; bedwetting; genital itching or swelling; swollen scrotum; somnolence, tired limbs; swollen neck lymph nodes
F 10.ci: Locate the femoral artery and needle beside it, without injuring it.

F 11.loc: On the medial thigh, 2 cun below ST 30.
F 11.act: Regulates the uterus and menstruation, promotes fertility, benefits the thigh.
F 11.ind: irregular menstruation; vaginal discharge; infertility; lower abdominal pain; thigh and leg pain; spasm of the inner thigh

F 12.loc: In the groin, level with the upper border of the pubic symphysis, 2.5 cun lateral to the anterior midline.
F 12.act: Spreads Liver Qi and frees the channel in the lower abdomen, benefits the genitals and relieves pain.
F 12.ind: hernia; genital pain; penile pain; uterine prolapse; lower abdominal pain; pain on the inner side of the thigh
F 12.ci: The femoral artery and vein are very close: needle with caution; classical texts favor moxibustion over needling on this point.

F 13.loc: On the side of the trunk, below the free end of the 11th rib.
F 13.act: Front-Mu point of the Spleen: harmonizes the Liver and Spleen.
F 13.fn: Harmonizes the Liver and Spleen, strengthens the Spleen, spreads Liver Qi, regulates the Middle Energizer and dissolves accumulations and masses.
F 13.locp: On the lateral abdomen, below the free end of the 11th rib.
F 13.ind: bloating; borborygmus; diarrhea with undigested food; vomiting; pain below the ribs; jaundice; abdominal masses; fatigue, weight loss; childhood malnutrition
F 13.ci: No deep needling: risk of injuring the liver (on the right) or the spleen (on the left), especially when enlarged.
cats: Hui-Meeting point of the Zang organs

F 14.loc: Below the nipple, in the 6th space between the ribs.
F 14.act: Front-Mu point of the Liver: frees Liver Qi, soothes the ribs.
F 14.fn: Spreads Liver Qi, harmonizes the Liver and Stomach, moves Blood, benefits the breasts and clears Heat that has entered the "Blood chamber".
F 14.locp: On the chest, in the 6th intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the anterior midline (usually directly below the nipple in men).
F 14.ind: pain and distension below the ribs; chest oppression, sighing; depressed mood; acid regurgitation; hiccups, vomiting; breast abscess; cough, asthma; fever and chills during menstruation
F 14.ci: Needle only obliquely or transversely: risk of pneumothorax and, on the right, of injury to the liver.

VG 1.loc: In the perineal region, below the coccyx, midway between the tip of the coccyx and the anus (patient prone or in knee-chest position).
VG 1.act: Regulates the Governing and Conception Vessels, drains Damp-Heat from the lower burner and treats hemorrhoids; calms the Shen and relieves pain of the coccyx and spine.
VG 1.ind: hemorrhoids; rectal prolapse; blood in the stool; diarrhea; constipation; coccyx and sacral pain; stiffness of the spine; bedwetting or urinary retention; anal itching; epilepsy; mental agitation
VG 1.ci: Needle obliquely upward, parallel to the front surface of the coccyx and sacrum: a perpendicular or overly deep insertion may perforate the rectum. Intimate area: explain the procedure and keep strict asepsis.
cats: Luo-Connecting point of the Governing Vessel

VG 2.loc: In the sacral region, on the posterior midline, at the sacral hiatus (the small depression just above the gluteal cleft).
VG 2.act: Strengthens the lower back and legs, expels Wind-Dampness and regulates the lower burner.
VG 2.ind: lumbosacral pain and stiffness; pain radiating down the leg; weakness, numbness or wasting of the legs; hemorrhoids; irregular menstruation; vaginal discharge; difficult urination; epilepsy

VG 3.loc: In the lumbar region, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of L4, level with the line joining the highest points of the iliac crests.
VG 3.act: Strengthens the lower back and knees, expels Wind-Cold-Dampness, warms Kidney Yang and strengthens the lower burner.
VG 3.ind: lower back pain; sciatic pain; knee pain and weakness; numbness or paralysis of the legs; impotence; seminal emission; irregular menstruation; vaginal discharge

VG 4.loc: On the lower back, on the midline, below the 2nd lumbar vertebra, at waist level.
VG 4.fn: Tonifies Kidney Yang and warms the Fire of the Gate of Life, nourishes Original Qi and Essence, strengthens the lower back, firms the lower burner (stops leakage such as diarrhea, discharge and bedwetting) and expels Cold.
VG 4.locp: In the lumbar region, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of L2 (roughly opposite the navel).
VG 4.ind: lower back pain with cold; impotence; premature ejaculation; seminal emission; infertility from Cold in the uterus; profuse clear vaginal discharge; frequent urination, bedwetting; early-morning diarrhea; feeling cold, cold limbs; tinnitus; deep fatigue

VG 5.loc: In the lumbar region, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of L1.
VG 5.act: Strengthens the back and lumbar spine, strengthens the Spleen and regulates the intestines.
VG 5.ind: lumbar stiffness and pain; diarrhea; undigested food in the stool; dysentery; abdominal pain; borborygmus; abdominal distension

VG 6.loc: On the back, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of T11.
VG 6.act: Strengthens the Spleen and drains Dampness, strengthens the spine and calms internal Wind (epilepsy).
VG 6.ind: diarrhea; jaundice; hemorrhoids; rectal prolapse; blood in the stool; abdominal distension; poor appetite; childhood malnutrition; stiffness and pain of the back; epilepsy
VG 6.ci: Moxibustion is classically forbidden on this point (old texts say it causes a hunched back). Needle obliquely upward, not too deep (spinal cord).

VG 7.loc: On the back, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of T10.
VG 7.act: Strengthens the Spleen and Stomach, strengthens the back and relieves pain.
VG 7.ind: back pain and stiffness; epigastric pain; vomiting; poor appetite; abdominal distension; jaundice; chills and fever
VG 7.ci: Needle obliquely upward and not too deep: risk of injuring the spinal cord.

VG 8.loc: On the back, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of T9.
VG 8.act: Soothes the Liver and extinguishes internal Wind, relaxes the tendons and muscles, calms spasms and the Shen.
VG 8.ind: epilepsy; convulsions; spasm and stiffness of the back; opisthotonos; muscle contractures; upward-staring eyes; agitation, mental disorders; epigastric pain; jaundice
VG 8.ci: Needle obliquely upward and not too deep: risk of injuring the spinal cord.

VG 9.loc: On the back, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of T7, level with the inferior angles of the shoulder blades (arms at the sides).
VG 9.act: Regulates the Liver and Gallbladder, drains Damp-Heat (jaundice), opens the chest and diaphragm and moves Qi.
VG 9.ind: jaundice; fullness of the chest and ribs; flank pain; cough, shortness of breath; epigastric pain; heavy body and limbs; back pain and stiffness; palpitations; fever
VG 9.ci: Needle obliquely upward and not too deep: risk of injuring the spinal cord.

VG 10.loc: On the back, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of T6.
VG 10.act: Clears Heat and toxic Heat (boils), makes Lung Qi descend, calms cough and wheezing, relieves the back.
VG 10.ind: boils and carbuncles; cough; asthma; fever; stiff neck; back pain and stiffness; epigastric pain
VG 10.ci: Classically forbidden to needling in some texts. Today it is needled obliquely upward, not too deep (spinal cord).

VG 11.loc: On the back, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of T5.
VG 11.act: Calms the Shen and settles the Heart, clears Heat, extinguishes Wind and strengthens the back.
VG 11.ind: palpitations; anxiety, fearfulness; insomnia; poor memory; sadness; epilepsy; childhood convulsions; fever with headache; cough; back stiffness and pain
VG 11.ci: Classically forbidden to needling in some texts. Today it is needled obliquely upward, not too deep (spinal cord).

VG 12.loc: On the midline of the back, below the 3rd thoracic vertebra.
VG 12.fn: Tonifies Lung Qi, clears Heat from the Lung and Heart, extinguishes Wind, calms the Shen and cough; strengthens the constitution of children (moxa).
VG 12.locp: On the upper back, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of T3, roughly level with the roots of the spines of the shoulder blades.
VG 12.ind: cough; asthma; fever; headache; childhood convulsions; epilepsy; agitation, mental disorders; back stiffness and pain; boils; weak constitution in children
VG 12.ci: Needle obliquely upward and not too deep: risk of injuring the spinal cord.

VG 13.loc: On the upper back, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of T1.
VG 13.act: Clears Heat, releases the exterior, harmonizes Shao Yang (alternating chills and fever) and calms the Shen.
VG 13.ind: fever; alternating chills and fever; malaria-like fever; aversion to cold; headache; stiffness of the neck and back; “bone-steaming” heat from Yin Deficiency; cough; sadness, low mood; epilepsy
VG 13.ci: Needle obliquely upward and not too deep: risk of injuring the spinal cord.

VG 14.loc: On the midline, below the most prominent vertebra at the base of the neck.
VG 14.act: Releases the surface, clears Heat, strengthens Yang.
VG 14.fn: Releases the exterior and expels Wind, clears Heat (Lung Heat, Deficiency fever), harmonizes the nutritive and defensive Qi, treats malaria, calms the Shen and tonifies Yang (moxa).
VG 14.locp: At the base of the neck, on the posterior midline, in the depression below the spinous process of C7 (the most prominent vertebra, which moves when the head is turned).
VG 14.ind: fever; common cold with aversion to cold; alternating chills and fever; cough, asthma; neck stiffness and pain; Deficiency fever, night sweats; epilepsy, convulsions; acne, hives; chronic fatigue, feeling cold
VG 14.ci: Needle slightly obliquely upward, no deeper than about 1 cun: deep insertion may reach the spinal cord.
cats: Meeting point of all Yang channels
Point of the Sea of Qi

VG 15.loc: At the back of the neck, on the posterior midline, in the depression above the spinous process of C2, 0.5 cun below GV 16 (about 0.5 cun above the posterior hairline).
VG 15.act: Frees the tongue and restores speech, clears the sense orifices and the Shen, expels Wind and relieves the neck.
VG 15.ind: loss of voice; aphasia after stroke; stiff tongue; deaf-mutism; epilepsy; mental disorders; occipital headache; stiff neck; nosebleed
VG 15.ci: Dangerous point: with the head slightly flexed, needle perpendicularly or toward the chin, 0.5 to 1 cun at most; never upward or deep (medulla oblongata, spinal cord). Moxibustion is classically forbidden (old texts say it causes muteness).
cats: Point of the Sea of Qi

VG 16.loc: At the back of the neck, on the posterior midline, just below the external occipital protuberance, in the depression between the two trapezius muscles (about 1 cun above the posterior hairline).
VG 16.act: Expels external Wind and extinguishes internal Wind, clears the head and sense orifices, calms the Shen, relieves the neck and throat.
VG 16.ind: occipital headache; dizziness; stiff neck; common cold with aversion to wind; sore throat; nosebleed; aphasia and hemiplegia after stroke; mental disorders; epilepsy; blurred vision
VG 16.ci: Dangerous point: with the head slightly flexed, needle toward the chin, 0.5 to 1 cun at most; never upward or deep (foramen magnum, medulla oblongata). Moxibustion is classically forbidden.
cats: Point of the Sea of Marrow
One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

VG 17.loc: On the head, on the posterior midline, in the depression above the external occipital protuberance, 1.5 cun above GV 16 (2.5 cun above the posterior hairline).
VG 17.act: Expels Wind, clears the head and eyes, calms the Shen and relieves pain.
VG 17.ind: occipital headache; heavy head; dizziness; stiff neck; eye pain; loss of voice; epilepsy; goiter
VG 17.ci: Needle only transversely under the scalp; several classical texts forbid deep needling and moxibustion on this point (moxa was said to cause muteness).

VG 18.loc: On the head, on the posterior midline, 4 cun above the posterior hairline (1.5 cun above GV 17).
VG 18.act: Calms the Shen, expels Wind and relieves the head and neck.
VG 18.ind: headache; dizziness; stiff neck; insomnia; agitation; mental disorders; epilepsy; vomiting

VG 19.loc: On the head, on the posterior midline, 5.5 cun above the posterior hairline (1.5 cun behind GV 20).
VG 19.act: Calms the Shen, expels Wind and relieves headache.
VG 19.ind: headache at the vertex and occiput; dizziness; stiff neck; insomnia; agitation; mental disorders; epilepsy

VG 20.loc: At the top of the head, where the midline crosses the line joining the tops of both ears.
VG 20.act: Lifts Qi, calms the mind, clears the head.
VG 20.fn: Raises Yang and Qi (prolapse), calms the Shen, clears the head and sense orifices, extinguishes internal Wind and subdues Liver Yang.
VG 20.locp: At the top of the head, on the midline, 5 cun behind the anterior hairline; landmark: the midpoint of the line joining the apexes of both ears (with the ears folded forward).
VG 20.ind: headache at the vertex; dizziness; rectal or uterine prolapse; hemorrhoids; chronic diarrhea; insomnia; poor memory; anxiety, depressed mood; after-effects of stroke; tinnitus; blocked nose
VG 20.ci: Moxibustion is not advised in Liver Yang rising or high blood pressure.
cats: Hundred Meetings: Yang channels meet at the head
Point of the Sea of Marrow

VG 21.loc: On the head, on the midline, 3.5 cun above the anterior hairline (midway between GV 20 and GV 22).
VG 21.act: Expels Wind, clears the head and calms convulsions.
VG 21.ind: headache at the vertex; dizziness; red, swollen face; facial edema; runny nose; childhood convulsions; epilepsy
VG 21.ci: In infants, do not needle until the anterior fontanelle has closed.

VG 22.loc: On the head, on the midline, 2 cun above the anterior hairline.
VG 22.act: Expels Wind, opens the nose, clears the head and calms the Shen.
VG 22.ind: headache; dizziness; blocked nose; runny nose, sinusitis; nosebleed; loss of smell; childhood convulsions; epilepsy; palpitations with fright
VG 22.ci: Forbidden in infants and young children until the anterior fontanelle has closed; classically forbidden to needling in some texts. In adults, needle transversely.

VG 23.loc: On the head, on the midline, 1 cun above the anterior hairline.
VG 23.act: Opens the nose, brightens the eyes, expels Wind, clears Heat and calms the Shen.
VG 23.ind: blocked nose; runny nose, rhinitis, sinusitis; nosebleed; loss of smell; frontal headache; red, painful eyes; facial edema; mental disorders
cats: One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

VG 24.loc: On the head, on the midline, 0.5 cun above the anterior hairline (if the hairline is unclear: 3.5 cun above the midpoint between the eyebrows).
VG 24.act: Calms the Shen and clears the mind, expels Wind, benefits the nose and eyes.
VG 24.ind: insomnia; anxiety; palpitations; poor memory; epilepsy; mental disorders; frontal headache; dizziness; rhinitis, runny nose; nosebleed; watery eyes
VG 24.ci: Classically forbidden to needling (old texts feared mental disturbance); today it is needled transversely and superficially.

VG 25.loc: On the face, at the tip of the nose.
VG 25.act: Clears Heat, opens the nose and restores consciousness.
VG 25.ind: blocked nose; rhinitis; nosebleed; nasal polyps; red nose (rosacea); loss of consciousness; shock; neonatal asphyxia
VG 25.ci: Moxibustion is classically forbidden. Painful point: needle superficially upward or prick to bleed.

VG 26.loc: On the upper lip, at the midpoint of the philtrum (WHO); traditional Chinese location: at the junction of the upper third and lower two thirds of the philtrum.
VG 26.act: Restores consciousness and calms the Shen, expels Wind from the face and relieves the lumbar spine in acute cases (point also called Ren Zhong).
VG 26.ind: loss of consciousness, fainting; coma; heatstroke; epilepsy, convulsions; acute agitation; acute lumbago (lower back sprain); facial paralysis; facial edema; blocked nose, nosebleed
VG 26.ci: Very painful point, needled obliquely upward; moxibustion is not advised on the lip. In loss of consciousness, call emergency services: the point does not replace first aid.
cats: One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

VG 27.loc: On the upper lip, at the midpoint of the tubercle of the lip, where the skin of the philtrum meets the red of the lip.
VG 27.act: Clears Heat, relieves the mouth and gums and calms the Shen.
VG 27.ind: swollen, painful gums; mouth ulcers; stiff or trembling lips; toothache; nosebleed; intense thirst (Xiao Ke); epilepsy; loss of consciousness
VG 27.ci: Moxibustion is not advised (lip); needle superficially and obliquely upward.

VG 28.loc: Inside the mouth, with the upper lip lifted: at the junction of the frenulum of the upper lip and the gum.
VG 28.act: Clears Heat, relieves the gums and nose, moves Qi in the Governing Vessel (acute lumbago).
VG 28.ind: swollen, painful or bleeding gums; bad breath; blocked nose, nasal polyps; red, watery eyes; acute lumbago; hemorrhoids; mental disorders
VG 28.ci: Point inside the mouth: superficial upward needling or pricking of small nodules on the frenulum; no moxibustion.

RM 1.loc: In the perineum, at the midpoint between the anus and the posterior border of the scrotum in men, or the posterior commissure of the labia majora in women (patient lying on the side).
RM 1.act: Regulates the front and back orifices, drains Damp-Heat, nourishes Yin, restores consciousness (drowning) and calms the Shen.
RM 1.ind: urinary retention, difficult urination; bedwetting; itching, pain or swelling of the genitals; hemorrhoids; rectal or uterine prolapse; irregular menstruation; seminal emission, impotence; loss of consciousness from drowning; mental disorders
RM 1.ci: Classically forbidden during pregnancy. Intimate area: explicit consent and strict asepsis; other points are often preferred.
cats: One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

RM 2.loc: On the lower abdomen, on the anterior midline, just above the upper border of the pubic symphysis, 5 cun below the navel.
RM 2.act: Promotes urination, regulates the lower burner, warms and tonifies the Kidney, regulates menstruation.
RM 2.ind: urinary retention; difficult or dribbling urination; bedwetting; vaginal discharge; irregular menstruation; painful periods; impotence; seminal emission; pain and fullness of the lower abdomen; hernia
RM 2.ci: Have the patient empty the bladder before needling (a full bladder can be punctured); not advised during pregnancy.

RM 3.loc: On the midline, 4 cun below the navel (1 cun above the pubic bone).
RM 3.act: Front-Mu point of the Bladder: regulates urination, eliminates Damp-Heat.
RM 3.fn: Supports the Bladder and promotes urination, drains Damp-Heat from the lower burner, regulates the uterus and menstruation, strengthens the Kidney.
RM 3.locp: On the lower abdomen, on the anterior midline, 4 cun below the navel (1 cun above the upper border of the pubic symphysis).
RM 3.ind: urinary retention; frequent, urgent or painful urination; bedwetting; vaginal discharge; irregular menstruation; painful periods; infertility; impotence; seminal emission; lower abdominal pain; genital itching
RM 3.ci: Have the patient empty the bladder before needling (a full bladder can be punctured); not advised during pregnancy.
cats: Meeting of the three leg Yin with the Conception Vessel

RM 4.loc: On the midline, 3 cun below the navel.
RM 4.act: Tonifies the Kidney, the original Qi and the Blood, grounds you.
RM 4.fn: Strengthens Original Qi and tonifies the Kidney, nourishes Blood and Yin, warms Yang (moxa), regulates the uterus and Small Intestine, roots the Hun.
RM 4.locp: On the lower abdomen, on the anterior midline, 3 cun below the navel.
RM 4.ind: fatigue and exhaustion; collapse (moxa); frequent urination, bedwetting; impotence, premature ejaculation; infertility; irregular or absent periods; painful periods; vaginal discharge; chronic diarrhea; lower abdominal pain; dizziness and tinnitus from Deficiency
RM 4.ci: Have the patient empty the bladder before needling; not advised during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy.
cats: Front-Mu point of the Small Intestine
Meeting of the three leg Yin with the Conception Vessel

RM 5.loc: On the lower abdomen, on the anterior midline, 2 cun below the navel.
RM 5.act: Moves fluids in the lower burner and promotes urination, regulates Qi, stops diarrhea and regulates the uterus.
RM 5.ind: edema; difficult urination; diarrhea; abdominal pain; hernia; lower abdominal distension; absent periods; vaginal discharge; uterine bleeding; postpartum hemorrhage
RM 5.ci: Classically not advised in women (old texts say it causes infertility) and forbidden during pregnancy.
cats: Front-Mu point of the Triple Energizer

RM 6.loc: On the midline, 1.5 cun below the navel.
RM 6.act: “Sea of Qi”: tonifies Qi and Yang.
RM 6.fn: Tonifies Qi and Yang, strengthens Original Qi and the Kidney, moves stagnant Qi in the lower abdomen and harmonizes Blood.
RM 6.locp: On the lower abdomen, on the anterior midline, 1.5 cun below the navel.
RM 6.ind: fatigue, exhaustion; shortness of breath; collapse; prolapse; abdominal distension and pain; diarrhea; constipation; bedwetting; impotence; irregular or absent periods; hernia
RM 6.ci: Not advised during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy; have the patient empty the bladder before needling.

RM 7.loc: On the lower abdomen, on the anterior midline, 1 cun below the navel.
RM 7.act: Regulates the Conception and Penetrating Vessels, regulates the uterus and menstruation, moves fluids.
RM 7.ind: irregular menstruation; uterine bleeding; vaginal discharge; infertility; postpartum pain; pain around the navel; hernia; edema; difficult urination; genital itching

RM 8.loc: At the center of the navel.
RM 8.act: Warms Yang and rescues collapsing Yang, strengthens the Spleen, regulates the intestines and stops diarrhea.
RM 8.ind: chronic diarrhea; undigested food in the stool; borborygmus; pain around the navel; rectal prolapse; collapse of Yang with cold limbs; collapse-type stroke; edema; infertility from Cold
RM 8.ci: Forbidden to needling. Indirect moxibustion only (on salt, on ginger or with a moxa stick), never a cone placed directly on the skin.

RM 9.loc: On the midline, 1 cun above the navel.
RM 9.fn: Regulates the water passages and promotes urination, harmonizes the Stomach and intestines.
RM 9.locp: On the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 1 cun above the navel.
RM 9.ind: edema, especially of the abdomen; ascites; difficult urination; borborygmus; diarrhea; abdominal pain; vomiting; back stiffness
RM 9.ci: In edema or ascites, classical texts prefer moxibustion to needling.

RM 10.loc: On the midline, 2 cun above the navel.
RM 10.act: Helps food move down from the Stomach to the intestine, relieves an overfull stomach.
RM 10.fn: Harmonizes the Stomach, makes Stomach Qi descend, dispels food stagnation and moves Qi.
RM 10.locp: On the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 2 cun above the navel.
RM 10.ind: food stagnation; epigastric or abdominal distension; epigastric pain; vomiting; undigested food in the stool; borborygmus; diarrhea; poor appetite; weight loss

RM 11.loc: On the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 3 cun above the navel.
RM 11.act: Harmonizes the middle burner, makes rebellious Qi descend, transforms Dampness and food stagnation.
RM 11.ind: epigastric pain; vomiting; poor appetite; abdominal distension; borborygmus; edema; heavy body; chest pain

RM 12.loc: On the midline, 4 cun above the navel, halfway between the navel and the base of the breastbone.
RM 12.act: Front-Mu point of the Stomach: tonifies and harmonizes the Stomach and Spleen, transforms Dampness.
RM 12.fn: Tonifies the Stomach and Spleen, harmonizes the middle burner, makes rebellious Stomach Qi descend, transforms Dampness and Phlegm.
RM 12.locp: On the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 4 cun above the navel, midway between the navel and the xiphisternal junction.
RM 12.ind: epigastric pain; abdominal distension; nausea, vomiting; acid reflux, belching; poor appetite; diarrhea; constipation; fatigue; cough with profuse Phlegm; insomnia from Stomach disharmony
cats: Hui-Meeting point of the Fu organs

RM 13.loc: On the midline, 5 cun above the navel (1 cun above CV 12).
RM 13.act: Makes Stomach Qi descend: belching, nausea, vomiting, overfull stomach.
RM 13.fn: Harmonizes the Stomach, makes rebellious Qi descend and dispels food stagnation.
RM 13.locp: On the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 5 cun above the navel.
RM 13.ind: vomiting; nausea; belching; hiccups; epigastric pain and fullness; acid reflux; poor appetite; abdominal distension; epilepsy

RM 14.loc: On the midline, 6 cun above the navel, just below the tip of the breastbone.
RM 14.act: Front-Mu point of the Heart: calms the mind, opens the chest.
RM 14.fn: Calms the Shen and regulates the Heart, transforms Phlegm, opens the chest, makes rebellious Stomach Qi descend.
RM 14.locp: On the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 6 cun above the navel (2 cun below the xiphisternal junction).
RM 14.ind: chest pain; palpitations; anxiety; agitation, mental disorders; epilepsy; oppression below the breastbone; vomiting; acid reflux; hiccups
RM 14.ci: Do not needle deeply or upward: risk of injuring the liver or heart, especially if either organ is enlarged.

RM 15.loc: On the midline, 1 cun below the tip of the breastbone (7 cun above the navel). Press gently.
RM 15.act: Luo point of the Conception Vessel: calms the mind, eases anxiety, nourishes the Heart.
RM 15.fn: Calms the Shen, settles the Heart, opens the chest and makes rebellious Qi descend.
RM 15.locp: On the upper abdomen, on the anterior midline, 1 cun below the xiphisternal junction (7 cun above the navel).
RM 15.ind: anxiety, distress; palpitations; mental disorders, epilepsy; insomnia; chest pain and oppression; cough, asthma; hiccups; vomiting; pain or itching of the abdominal skin
RM 15.ci: Needle obliquely downward, never deep or upward (heart, liver). Moxibustion is classically forbidden.
cats: Luo-Connecting point of the Conception Vessel

RM 16.loc: On the chest, on the anterior midline, at the midpoint of the xiphisternal junction.
RM 16.act: Opens the chest, moves Qi and makes rebellious Qi descend.
RM 16.ind: fullness of the chest and ribs; vomiting after meals; difficulty swallowing; milk regurgitation in infants; hiccups; discomfort in the throat

RM 17.loc: In the middle of the breastbone, between the two nipples.
RM 17.act: Meeting point of Qi: opens the chest, regulates breathing.
RM 17.fn: Regulates and moves Qi, opens the chest, makes rebellious Lung and Stomach Qi descend, transforms Phlegm and promotes lactation.
RM 17.locp: On the breastbone, on the anterior midline, level with the 4th intercostal space (between the nipples in men).
RM 17.ind: chest oppression; chest pain; shortness of breath; asthma, cough; palpitations; insufficient breast milk; breast pain or abscess; hiccups; difficulty swallowing; frequent sighing
RM 17.ci: Needle only transversely: some people have a hole in the breastbone (sternal foramen) that exposes the heart to perpendicular needling. Classically forbidden to needling in some texts.
cats: Point of the Sea of Qi

RM 18.loc: On the breastbone, on the anterior midline, level with the 3rd intercostal space.
RM 18.act: Opens the chest, moves Qi and calms cough.
RM 18.ind: chest pain and oppression; cough; asthma; shortness of breath; vomiting; breast pain or swelling; sore throat

RM 19.loc: On the breastbone, on the anterior midline, level with the 2nd intercostal space.
RM 19.act: Opens the chest, makes Lung Qi descend and calms cough.
RM 19.ind: cough; asthma; chest pain; sore throat; vomiting; difficulty swallowing; poor appetite

RM 20.loc: On the breastbone, on the anterior midline, level with the 1st intercostal space.
RM 20.act: Makes Lung Qi descend, opens the chest and relieves the throat.
RM 20.ind: cough; asthma; shortness of breath; chest pain and fullness; sore, swollen throat; rib pain

RM 21.loc: On the manubrium of the breastbone, on the anterior midline, 1 cun below the suprasternal fossa (1 cun below CV 22).
RM 21.act: Makes Lung and Stomach Qi descend, opens the chest, relieves the throat and dispels food stagnation.
RM 21.ind: cough; asthma; chest pain; sore throat; swollen throat; food stagnation; epigastric fullness

RM 22.loc: In the center of the hollow above the breastbone. Press gently downward, never toward the throat.
RM 22.act: Makes Lung Qi descend, loosens the throat, calms coughing.
RM 22.fn: Makes Lung Qi descend and calms cough and wheezing, transforms Phlegm, relieves the throat and voice, makes rebellious Qi descend.
RM 22.locp: At the base of the neck, on the anterior midline, at the center of the suprasternal fossa (the hollow above the manubrium of the breastbone).
RM 22.ind: cough; asthma; Phlegm in the throat; sore throat; hoarseness, loss of voice; sensation of a lump in the throat; goiter; hiccups; difficulty swallowing; vomiting
RM 22.ci: Delicate point: first insert perpendicularly 0.2 to 0.3 cun, then direct the needle downward behind the breastbone, never sideways or backward (trachea, aorta, large vessels, pleura). For acupressure, press gently downward.

RM 23.loc: On the neck, on the anterior midline, with the head slightly tilted back: above the thyroid cartilage, in the depression above the upper border of the hyoid bone.
RM 23.act: Frees the tongue and restores speech, makes Qi descend, transforms Phlegm and clears Heat.
RM 23.ind: stiff tongue; aphasia after stroke; swelling under the tongue; drooling; sore throat; sudden loss of voice; difficulty swallowing; cough, asthma; mouth ulcers; loss of taste

RM 24.loc: On the face, in the depression at the center of the groove between the lower lip and the chin (mentolabial sulcus).
RM 24.act: Expels Wind from the face, relieves the mouth and teeth, regulates the Conception Vessel.
RM 24.ind: facial paralysis; deviated mouth; toothache; swollen gums; drooling; mouth ulcers; facial swelling; stiff neck; intense thirst (Xiao Ke); epilepsy
cats: Meeting of the Conception Vessel, Governing Vessel and Stomach
One of Sun Simiao's 13 Ghost points

Yin Tang.loc: Between the eyebrows, in the middle.
Yin Tang.act: Calms the mind, helps sleep, soothes the forehead and nose.
Yin Tang.fn: Calms the Shen, expels Wind, opens the nose, clears the head and eyes.
Yin Tang.locp: On the forehead, at the midpoint between the inner ends of the eyebrows.
Yin Tang.ind: insomnia; anxiety, restlessness; frontal headache; dizziness; blocked nose, rhinitis; sinusitis; nosebleed; eye pain; childhood convulsions
Yin Tang.ci: Needle transversely downward while pinching up the skin. Moxibustion is not advised (close to the eyes).

Tai Yang.loc: In the hollow of the temple, 1 cun behind the point midway between the end of the eyebrow and the outer corner of the eye.
Tai Yang.act: Eases headaches at the temples and soothes the eyes.
Tai Yang.fn: Expels Wind, clears Heat, reduces swelling, relieves pain and brightens the eyes.
Tai Yang.locp: At the temple, in the depression about 1 cun (one finger-width) behind the midpoint between the outer end of the eyebrow and the outer corner of the eye.
Tai Yang.ind: temporal headache; migraine; red, swollen, painful eyes; eye strain; dizziness; facial paralysis; facial (trigeminal) neuralgia; toothache
Tai Yang.ci: Close to the superficial temporal artery: needle superficially, perpendicularly or obliquely backward; pricking to bleed is possible. Moxibustion is not advised (close to the eye).

An Mian.loc: Behind the ear, halfway between TE 17 and GB 20.
An Mian.act: “Peaceful Sleep”: calms the mind, helps you fall asleep.
An Mian.fn: Calms the Shen, subdues Liver Yang and extinguishes Wind.
An Mian.locp: Behind the ear, at the midpoint of the line joining TE 17 (behind the earlobe) and GB 20 (below the occiput).
An Mian.ind: insomnia; restless sleep; dizziness; headache; palpitations; restlessness, irritability; high blood pressure; mental disorders

Ding Chuan.loc: 0.5 cun on each side of the most prominent vertebra at the base of the neck.
Ding Chuan.fn: Makes Lung Qi descend, calms wheezing and cough.
Ding Chuan.locp: On the upper back, 0.5 cun to each side of the lower border of the spinous process of C7 (on either side of GV 14).
Ding Chuan.ind: asthma; wheezing; cough; bronchitis; hives; stiff neck; pain of the shoulders and upper back
Ding Chuan.ci: Needle perpendicularly or slightly toward the spine, not too deep and never angled outward (pleura).

Nei Xi Yan.loc: Knee bent, in the hollow below the kneecap, on the inner side of the kneecap tendon.
Nei Xi Yan.act: Soothes the knee, expels local Cold and Dampness.
Nei Xi Yan.fn: Expels Wind, Cold and Dampness, moves Qi and Blood, relieves pain and strengthens the knee.
Nei Xi Yan.locp: With the knee bent, in the depression below the kneecap, medial to the patellar ligament; the matching hollow lateral to the ligament is ST 35.
Nei Xi Yan.ind: knee pain; knee swelling; stiffness and difficulty bending the knee; cold knee; weak legs; knee osteoarthritis
Nei Xi Yan.ci: Needle obliquely toward the center of the knee; the joint is close: strict asepsis (risk of joint infection).

He Ding.loc: Above the kneecap, in the hollow at the middle of its upper edge.
He Ding.act: Moves Qi and Blood in the knee.
He Ding.fn: Moves Qi and Blood in the knee, expels Wind-Dampness and strengthens the legs.
He Ding.locp: Above the knee, in the depression at the midpoint of the upper border of the kneecap (knee slightly bent).
He Ding.ind: knee pain; knee swelling; weak legs; difficulty walking; paralysis of the legs; wasting of the thigh muscles

Bai Chong Wo.loc: Knee bent, 3 cun above the upper inner corner of the kneecap (1 cun above SP 10).
Bai Chong Wo.act: “Nest of a Hundred Insects”: calms itching.
Bai Chong Wo.fn: Clears Heat from the Blood, expels Wind, stops itching and expels parasites.
Bai Chong Wo.locp: With the knee bent, on the inner thigh, 3 cun above the upper inner corner of the kneecap, that is 1 cun above SP 10.
Bai Chong Wo.ind: itching; hives; eczema; skin rashes; genital itching; intestinal parasites

Zi Gong.loc: 4 cun below the navel, 3 cun on each side of the midline.
Zi Gong.fn: Raises Qi and holds the uterus (prolapse), regulates menstruation and supports fertility.
Zi Gong.locp: On the lower abdomen, 4 cun below the navel and 3 cun to each side of the midline (level with CV 3).
Zi Gong.ind: uterine prolapse; infertility; irregular menstruation; painful periods; uterine bleeding; vaginal discharge; lower abdominal pain
Zi Gong.ci: Forbidden during pregnancy; have the patient empty the bladder before needling.

Ah Shi.loc: The most tender point or points when you press around the painful area. Search with your thumb: you'll know you've found it when you say “ah, that's it”.
Ah Shi.fn: Moves Qi and Blood locally, unblocks the channels and collaterals, relieves pain.
Ah Shi.locp: No fixed location: it is the most tender spot found by palpation, on or near the painful area, on a channel or off it (“where it hurts is the point”). It is recognized by the patient's reaction: “Ah, that's it!”
Ah Shi.ind: localized pain; muscle tension and contractures; sprains; Bi syndrome (joint pain from Wind, Cold or Dampness); joint stiffness; trigger points
Ah Shi.ci: Do not needle or press hard over a tumor, infection, wound, recent fracture, varicose vein or phlebitis; follow the precautions of the area (chest, abdomen in pregnancy, large vessels, eye). Unexplained or persistent pain should be checked by a doctor.
